transcript: Not much later, as Picard stared out one of the ports in the Enterprise's observation lounge, three of his officers filed into the room. Later on, the Enterprise was going to pick up additional personnel at Farpoint Station, but for now, he would make do with Lieutenant Yarr, Councillor Troy, and Lieutenant Worf. He took a seat at the head of the polished synthetic wood table, a moment later the others followed suit. In the future, he would come to know these people well. He would come to trust them implicitly. For the time being, however, he eyed them warily, and they looked at him the same way. He asked Lieutenant Yarr to report. Sir, we've completed a full subspace scan of the ship and surrounding space we detected no unusual readings or anomalies. Worf spoke up. With all due respect, sir, it would help if we knew what we were looking for. Picard nodded. Your comment is noted, Mr. Worf. Picard turned to the Batazoid, or more accurately half Batazoid, since her father had been human. Councillor Troy, would you sense anything unusual aboard the Enterprise? Say, an alien presence that doesn't belong here? Troy applied her empathic powers, a little while later, she shook her head. No, sir. I'm only aware of the crew and the families aboard the ship, of course. Getting up, Picard took a few steps around the table. He knew that their eyes were on him. Mr. Worf, I want you to initiate a level two security alert on all decks until further notice. The Klingon looked surprised. As the captain watched, Worf glanced at Yarr, an awkward expression on his face. Clearly, Yarr was perturbed. Sir, with all due respect, I'm the security chief on this ship, unless you're planning to make a change, that is. Picard cursed inwardly. She was right, of course. It was just that his instinct was to think of Worf as the security chief. No, Lieutenant. I'm planning no such thing. Security alert, level two, Lieutenant. Captain Picard to the bridge, please. Picard knew the voice. It belonged to O'Brien, to whom he'd assigned primary Khan duties. Picard and the officers left for the bridge. There they saw Miles O'Brien, a rather likable Irishman, waiting for them in the command area with a pad in his hand. As Picard approached, O'Brien extended it to him. Star Fleet has just issued an alert, sir. It appears a number of vessels are moving toward the neutral zone between Romulan and Federation's space. That news caught Tasha's interest. What kind of vessels? O'Brien turned to her. Frater's transport is all civilian. None of them federationships. As Picard read the specifics on the pad he frowned, it says that a large spatial anomaly has appeared in the neutral zone, in the Devron system. Worf's response was quick and heated, no surprise, given his racial heritage. The Klingons and the Romulans, once allies, were now the most vicious of enemies. Perhaps it is a Romulan trick. A plan to lure ships into the neutral zone as an excuse for a military strike. O'Brien eyed the Klingon. I don't know about that, sir. But Star Fleet's cancelling out our mission to Faroe Point Station and ordering us to the neutral zone as soon as we can leave space-stock. To Tasha that news wasn't all bad. Sitting here in Drydock had made her edgy, irritable. She couldn't wait to put this new ship of theirs through its paces. As far as she was concerned, the neutral zone was as good a place to do that as any. Picard looked up from the pad. We will not go to the neutral zone. We will proceed to Faroe Point as planned. Tasha looked at him. She began to object, but Worf beat her to it. Captain, the security of the Federation may be at stake. Picard silenced him with a glance. Manual Station, Mr. Worf, or I will find someone who can. Troy frowned. Captain, perhaps if we understood your thinking, if you could explain. Unflappable, Picard shook his head. I don't intend to explain anything, Consular. We will proceed to Faroe Point Station as I indicated. Picard turned to O'Brien. Now, if I'm not a mistaken chief, we're having some problems with the warp plasma and doosas. O'Brien seemed surprised. That's right, sir, but how did you know? Never mind that, Chief. I think I know a way to get them back online. Lieutenant Jarr, the chief and I will be in main engineering if you need one of us. Tasha nodded and watched the two of them exit into the Turbulift. No sooner were they gone than she saw Worf make his way toward her. I do not understand. The Romulans may be planning an attack and he does not seem to care. What are you going to do? I'm going to do what I'm told, Mr. Worf, and prepare to go to Faroe Point. That was obviously not the response Worf wanted to hear. Still, it was the only one Tasha was prepared to make for now. Picard sat in the chief engineer's office at a console with Miles O'Brien standing beside him, handing O'Brien a pad to Captain sat back in his chair. I've bypassed the secondary plasma and doofa chief. Now I want to begin realigning the power grid to the specifications I've given you any questions. O'Brien looked less than confident. You have to realize, sir, this isn't exactly my area of expertise. Chief, trust me. I know you can do this. All those years you spent as a child building model starship engines represented time well spent. O'Brien stared at him as if Picard had just confessed to being a forrengi on his mother's side. How did you know that, sir? Abruptly, Picard realized that he'd put his foot in his mouth. O'Brien had confided that information to him in a conversation that wouldn't take place until years hence. Picard cleared his throat to cover his reaction. From your Starfleet records, Chief, where else could I have learned such a thing? Really, sir, I didn't think anyone studied those things so closely. Picard was relieved that O'Brien believed him. Now, Chief, about that power grid. Yes, sir, I'll get right on it. Taking the pad, O'Brien headed across the engineering section. Picard looked again at the chief engineer's monitor to check the schematics, and he felt a slight dizziness. Picard blinked and found himself staring at a darkened monitor. Looking around, he saw that he was in Dr. Crusher's office back in what he had come to think of as the present. He was still in his bathrobe. He turned to see Beverly standing at the entrance to the office. Jean-Luc, what's going on? Riker was standing behind her, his eyes asking the same question that the doctor had asked out loud. It happened again. A time shift. She held up a hand. Don't move. She disappeared, and a moment later she came back with a medical tricorder and used it to scan Picard's head. Riker looked worried. What happened, Captain? It's a little vague, number one. But I can remember more of it this time. I think the more often I shift between time periods of the more memory I retain. First, I was in what appeared to be the future years from now. Then I was in the past again, right before our first mission. Having finished her scan, Beverly read the results and shook her head in disbelief. I scanned his temporal lobe and compared it with what I found just a few minutes ago. There's a 13% increase in neurotransmitter activity in a hippocampus. Within a matter of minutes you accumulated over two days worth of memories. Riker frowned. Two days. But that's impossible. Picard smiled grimly. Unless you've spent a lot of time somewhere else between ticks of the clock. Then he sighed with relief. Finally they had some proof of what he was experiencing. He wasn't crazy enough. He was actively traveling through time. In the observation lounge, Riker shook his head as he sat in his customary place at the dark reflective table, surrounded by the ships, other senior officers. The idea that the captain was traveling through time, the victim of some capricious agency as yet beyond their understanding. It was bizarre to say the least, and more than a little unsettling. As he gazed at Picard, he had the feeling that the captain might pop in and out of their reality at any time. An entire journey, perhaps two or three days worth, completed in the space of an idling. They'd had their run-ins with time before. But he might have felt better if they'd had a little more to go on. Some data they could sink their collective teeth into. But then that was the purpose of this meeting, wasn't it? To see what they could nail down with regard to Picard's time shifting. And then to see what, if anything, they could do about it. Picard addressed them. Thank you all for being prompt. He turned to Troy. Councillor, do you remember the first day I came aboard the Enterprise? Yes, Captain, I think I do. Picard leaned forward. What happened after the welcoming ceremony? Troy thought for a moment. There was a reception in ten forward. I introduced you to Worf and the other senior officers. Picard held his hand up to stop her. Do you have any memory of me calling for a red alert in shuttle bay? Do you remember Starfleet diverting us from far point to the neutral zone to investigate a spatial anomaly? She thought again. No, Captain, I don't. Picard leaned back in his chair. As you may have gathered, I do have that memory. I experienced those events just a few short hours ago. Data ventured an observation. It would appear that there is a discontinuity between the time periods you have described. Events in one period would seem to have no effect on the other two. Riker then commented. And yet in both the past and the present, there's a report of the same anomaly in the Devron system. It's hard for me to believe that's a coincidence. Picard nodded. And for all I know, there may be a similar anomaly in the future as well. Le Forge added his thoughts. Maybe the anomaly is some kind of temporal disruption, a hole in the continuum. Crusher turned to Picard. But how is all this related to your time shifting? A good question, Dr. Crusher. I suspect I may have some answers when I make my next round trip to the past. Or the future, whichever comes first. Riker spoke up. In the meantime, we've got the Romulans to keep us from getting bored. Picard turned to him. Thank you for reminding me, number one. And so far as the current mission is concerned, all departments should submit combat readiness reports by 0-800 hours tomorrow. Dismissed. Everyone rose to go intent on their respective assignments. As Troy headed for the door, Riker caught her attention. Looks like it's going to be a late night. Want to get some dinner? He saw something in her eyes that he hadn't quite expected. A hesitation. Actually, will I, I mean, we have plans. She glanced over his shoulder and he turned to follower Gaze. He found himself looking at Worf. Apparently the relationship between Deanna and Worf had progressed further than he realized. Oh, I see. Well, then, I'll see you both tomorrow morning. He stood there for a moment watching the two of them file out after the others and felt an emptiness in the pit of his belly. Not that he had any right to tell either of them whom they could spend their time with. Even though he and Deanna hadn't been lovers for several years now, since his assignment on Betazoid came to an end, he'd always thought of her as his special friend. And now he saw that someone else might be taking his place in that regard. Someone he liked and respected, true. But it was still a change he wasn't looking forward to. Or was there more to it than that? That his feelings run deeper than he cared to admit. At some level, had he harbored the hope that in the end, he and Deanna would wind up together again? Beliegered by such disturbing thoughts he saw and he went back out onto the bridge. On the bridge of the Enterprise, Picard paused by the aft science station. Commander Deanna, I want continuous subspace sweeps we might detect a temporal disturbance. Without hesitation, Deanna got to work manipulating his instruments. Seeing that Riker was headed for the empty command area, Picard joined him. Will, this time shifting business, when it happens, I experience a moment of disorientation. If this should occur during a crisis, I want you to be ready to take command immediately. Picard got no reaction from his first officer who had a far away look on his face. A abruptly Riker realized that the captain was looking at him. He straightened in his seat. Sorry Captain, be prepared to take command, I sir. The captain frowned. Speaking of disorientation, are you alright? Well, the first officer nodded reassuringly. Just a little distracted. I'm fine sir, really. Then you have the bridge number one. I'll be in my ready room. Rising the captain made his way to his ready room door. As never before, he was grateful for the sanctum-like nature of it. His steady, predictable peacefulness. Everything was right where he expected it to be. From his antique Shakespearean folio, to his model of the stargazer, he moved to the couch and stretched out. He could hear his joints creak with gratitude. Closing his eyes, he assured himself that it would only be a short nap. And he began to drift off. He thought he heard a voice, but that was ridiculous, he was alone. Sir, wake up sir! Opening his eyes, Picard saw that Le Forge was standing over him. Jordi, what is it? Have we reached the neutral zone yet? Le Forge scrutinized him with his artificial eyes. The neutral zone captain? That's when Picard sat up and looked around and realized that he was back in DETA's library, in the future. Sorry, Jordi. I was in the past again. What's going on here? Le Forge smiled sympathetically. DETA's arranged for us to run some tests on you in the biometrics lab. We're ready to go if you are. The card shook his head, remembering what he'd learned. No, no, no, no, we don't have time for that. We have to get to the neutral zone. Le Forge's forehead wrinkled. Why is that, sir? The older Picard tried to concentrate. In the other two time periods, Starfleet reported some kind of spatial anomaly in the DETA system. That's it, the DETA system in the neutral zone. If the anomaly was in the past, it might be here to we need. We need to go find out. Le Forge looked at him as scans. Just because you've seen it in two other time frames doesn't mean it's going to be here. Picard felt the blood rush to his face. Dammit, Jordi. I know what we have to do. Okay, captain, whatever you say. But first of all, there is no neutral zone. Remember, the card pondered the matter, plumbing his memory. Yes, Jordi, you're right. In this time period, the Klingons have taken over the Romulan Empire. That's right, captain. And relations between us and the Klingons aren't real cozy right now. Getting irritated at Le Forge's tone, the older Picard struggled to his feet. I know that. I haven't completely lost my mind, you know. Abruptly, it occurred to him how cantankerous he sounded. Hoping to take the edge off his remark, he put his hand on Le Forge's shoulder. Sorry, Jordi. When I'm here, it's hard for me to concentrate and remember things. I don't mean to take out that frustration on you. It's okay, captain. Well, if we're going to go to the DETA system, we're going to need a ship. Picard scratched his chin. We will it at? I think it's time to call in some old favors. Let's contact Admiral Riker at Starbase 24-7. A seeding to Picard's request, DETA brought a Starfleet monitor into the library. He didn't take him long to contact Starfleet Command into a range for an audience with Admiral Riker. Only minutes after DETA had made his request, Riker got in touch with him. He was a lot greater than any of them remembered. But that wasn't the only difference. Even before Riker opened his mouth to speak, he seemed brittle somehow. Less easygoing than the man they'd known on the Enterprise. And there was no trace at all that trademark Will Riker smiled. Riker nodded curtly to acknowledge his former shipmates and captain. He was clearly pleased to see them, but he almost seemed leery at what it might be about. Picard looked at Riker with pride. Well, you look every into the Admiral. I knew we'd move you up in the ranks eventually. Riker shifted uncomfortably in his seat. Of course you did. Now, what can I do for you, sir? As Picard outlined his needs and the reasons for them, Riker's demeanor became frostier by degrees. Finally, he sat back in his chair and frowned. Captain, you know I'd like to help, but frankly what you're asking for is impossible. The Klingons have closed their borders to all Federation starships. Obviously trying to remain patient, Picard shook his head. I don't think you appreciate the gravity of the situation, Will. If this spatial anomaly really is the Devron system, Riker didn't let him finish. I saw a report from Starfleet Intelligence on that sector this morning. There's no unusual activity in the Devron system, nothing out of the ordinary in terms of celestial phenomena. Picard got irritated. I don't believe that. Maybe the long-range scan is a flawed. We have to go there, see for ourselves. Riker looked reluctant to turn Picard down flat. The eye data. Professor, what do you make of all this? Data seemed to hesitate for a moment, considering his answer carefully. I am not certain, however, I cannot disprove what the captain is saying, and he seems to be convinced he is traveling back and forth through time. Riker frowned. Clearly, Data was sighting with Picard, and that made it harder for him to dismiss the matter. Look, I've got the Yorktown out near the border. I'll have Captain Shelby running some long-range scans in the Devron system. If she finds anything, I'll let you know. Picard shook his head. No. That's not good enough. It'll have to be, I'm sorry, Captain. That's all I can do. Riker out. As the communication with Riker came to an end, Jordi knew it wasn't going to sit well with the captain. But on the other hand, it was clearly for the best. After all, they had no business trying to make their way through Klingon territory. They would have been risking a lot to satisfy an old man's fantasy. Picard turned his back on the monitor. Damn him, anyway. Ungrateful young pup. He's been sitting behind that desk too long. Do you know how many times I pulled his chestnuts out of their fire, do you? Leforj tried hard to mask his relief. I guess all we can do now is wait and see if the Yorktown finds anything. Data looked at them both. There is another option. We could arrange passage aboard a medical ship. There was an outbreak of Terellian Plague on Romulus. The Klingon High Council has been allowing Federation medical ships to cross the border. Leforj eyed data. It looked like this was going to go on after all. Picard grabbed data by the arm. I think I've got a range that Mr. Data finds the USS past year. I have some... some pole with her commanding officer. For a moment, Picard seemed lost and thought his eyes glazed over with memories. And it came out of it. At least I used to have some pole. The Doctor Beverly Picard, captain of the medical vessel known as the USS past year, considered all three of the visitors standing there in her ready room. However, she focused most of her attention on the man she had once called her husband. I never could say no to you Jean-Luc. He smiled. You should have said it when I asked you to marry me. Beverly looked at him with mock annoyance. Don't bring that up or I'll change my mind about all this. For a moment, a scene flashed before her eyes. She saw herself on her wedding day. She and Jean-Luc were taking their vows as their friends and fellow officers looked on. And she was truly happy for the first time in many years. She vowed on that special day the marriage would last. So much for her powers of prognostication. It was a good thing she was a doctor and not a fortune teller. Picard elbowed data in his synthetic ribs. You see, I knew I could still count on her, not like a raker. Did I tell you what he said to me, Beverly? To me? She nodded. You told me, Jean-Luc. It hurt her to see him like this. A man whose intellect was once so engaging, reduced now to near-senality. She took in Jorri and then data with a glance. Well then, the first order of businesses to obtain clearance to cross the Klingon border. And believe me, that won't be easy. La Forge rubbed his chin. What about Worf? Isn't he still on the Klingon High Council? Data's face registered doubt. I'm not sure. Information on the Klingon political structure is hard to come by these days. However, at last report, Worf was living on Hatoria, a small Klingon colony near the border. Picard snapped his fingers. Worf, yes, that's it. That's the answer. Kill Helpus. Make it so. Chilton to the captain. McKinley's station is signaling. They want to know when we'll be docking. Beverly stood. Tell McKinley that we've been called away on a priority mission. We won't be docking any time soon. Beverly led Picard and his companions out onto the bridge. If his judgment can be trusted, the medical ship would have a slightly different purpose. But they would still be saving lives. She addressed Ensign Chilton. Lay in a course for Hatoria. Best speed. Turning to Picard, Beverly gestured to the Turbulift. I prepared quarters for you on deck five if you'd like some rest. He gave her a sour look. You go again, always telling me to get some rest. I wanted a wife, not a personal physician. Spiling cordially, she reminded him of where he was and who was in charge here. Jean-Luc, I could have you escorted there. He turned his back on her. I can find my way around a starship, Beverly. I'm not that old. And grumbling all the way, he entered the Turbulift. Inside the lift, Picard fixed his objective in his mind. I got to find that anomaly. Show them all I'm not crazy. They'll see. Not that he cared all that much about being proven right, that would just be the icing on the cake. But he really wanted to find out why he was shifting through time and what it had to do with the phenomenon in the Devron system. Abruptly, the lift stopped and the doors opened. He stepped out, feeling dizzy again. He was back on the bridge. Then he realized that once again, he'd been transported in time. He saw Tasha, a tactical wharf at an after station, O'Brien at Khan and Data at Ops. Troy was sitting in her customary seat beside the captain's chair. Pulling down on the front of his tunic, Picard entoned. Report? Troy replied. We're on course for a far point. We should arrive in approximately 14 hours, 30 minutes. Picard nodded, moving to O'Brien's side. He gazed over the man's shoulder at the helm's monitors. Chief, how far are we from the Chaves system? The Chaves system we just passed it, sir. Picard couldn't quite believe his ears. Past it. And nothing happened. Nothing, sir. Picard silently cursed to himself, then gave his orders. Drop out of warpers to O'Brien, reverse course, take us back to the Chaves system. He could see the reactions through his directive out of the corner of his eye. Tasha, Troy and several others were having a hard time figuring him out. O'Brien, however, simply did as he was told. It took several minutes for them to come about and return to the court and its Picard had in mind. Of course, considering the circumstances, it seemed like much longer. Finally, the chief spoke up again. We've entered the Chaves system, sir. The captain turned to Data. Commander, is there anything unusual in the vicinity? Data looked back at him. How would you define unusual, sir? Every region of space has unique properties that cannot be found anywhere else. Picard thought about it and finally came up with something. There should be a baddie of some sort. A lot plasma feel highly disruptive. Tasha worked at her tactical board after a while she shook her head. Nothing, sir. Frustrated, the captain looked down again at O'Brien's console. It's the right time. The right place. He should be here. O'Brien's brow-puckard. Who, sir? Straightening Picard looked around the bridge and called out. Q, we're here, dammit. This has gone on long enough. What sort of game are you playing? There was no response, at least not from Q. However, the bridge crew was responding. They were exchanging glances from one to the other, no doubt, starting to wonder about their captain's insanity. Frowning, Picard turned to Troy. Counselor, do sense an alien presence, a superior intelligence. She looked worried. No, sir. This is not the way it's supposed to happen. Maintain position here. I'll be in my ready room. En route, he endured his officers' stairs without a word. What could he say, after all, that the super intelligent being he'd been expecting hadn't shown up? That he'd diverged from Starfleet orders to lead them on some kind of wild goose chase? Disgusted, he entered his ready room, but found himself in a different place entirely. It was a courtroom of sorts made of glass and steel without a single surface that wasn't hard and unyielding. The crowd was packed into the place, a gallery of leering, hollow-eyed scarecrows. Men and women who pointed at him and shrieked his name. Among them were the haggard souls he had seen in the vineyards of his future, and the shuttle bay of his past. Except their numbers had vastly multiplied. The air was ranked with their scent, with their hatred and desperation. Suddenly, he knew where he was and when. He had been here before, after all. The time was the 21st century, the era of mankind's post-atomic horror. That explained the hunger and the poverty that characterized the spectators, the bitterness in their voices, the hopelessness in their eyes. And this venue was the one in which he had been placed on trial several years earlier. Not just him alone either, but all of humanity. As if to confirm his suspicions, everyone looked in one direction at once, at an entrance to the room, approachable only through a long, dark hallway. There was someone making his way down that hallway now, someone sitting cross-legged on a floating chair. With impeccable timing, Q emerged from the shadows playing the crowd like a virtuosan. The haggard ones roared their approval as Q wafted out to the center of the room, wearing an elaborate set of judges' robes. Holding his hand up, he quieted the cheering throng. His eyes twinkling with irony, Q turned to Picard. Mon capitan! I thought you'd never get here! Picard had no patience for Q's antics. What's going on, Q? Q made an expansive gesture indicating the entire courtroom and its cadre of foul-smelling occupants. Isn't it obvious, Jean-Luc, can't you see for yourself, old bean? Or is a little simple cognition beyond you? The card saw he would have to play the game like it or not. Q, the last time I stood in this courtroom was seven years ago. Q smiled and repeated mockingly. Seven years ago, how little you mortals understand, time. Must you be so linear, Jean-Luc? Doggedly, Picard went on. You accused me of being the representative of a barbarous species. Jean-Luc, I believe the exact words were a dangerous, savage child race. Were they not? Picard ignored the interruption, but we demonstrated that mankind has become peaceful and benevolent. Why do I find myself back in this courtroom now, when our business here is finished? Q sighed. You need me to connect the dots for you, I see, so your puny mind can comprehend. It would be so much more entertaining if you tried to figure this out. He snapped his fingers, his eyes widening as if seized all of a sudden by an idea. Here's the deal, Mon ami. I'll answer any question that calls for a yes or a no. Put it together in ten questions or less, and you, a Jean-Luc Picard, could be our big winner. What do you say? Picard didn't seem to have much of a choice. All right, Q, my first question. Is there any connection at all between the trials seven years ago and whatever's going on now? Q pretended to think about it. Now, let's see. Hmm. I would have to say, yes. Picard concentrated on his next question. This spatial anomaly in the neutral zone, is it related to what's happening? Oh, most definite, yes. Is it part of a rameleon plot? Appoiced Star of War. Jean-Luc, you've been spending too much time with the Klingon. The answers are no and no again, four down and only six to go. Picard held his anger in check. Did you create the anomaly, Q? No, no, no, my incredible dullard of a starship, Captain. You're going to be surprised when you realize where it came from. That is, if you ever managed to figure it out. Picard decided to try another tack. Are you responsible for my shifting through time? Q looked around as if he was about to do something illegal and was concerned that someone might be watching. He leaned it down from his perch atop the floating cushion. I'll answer that, but you must not tell anyone. The answer is, yes. But why, Q? I'm sorry, Captain. That's not a yes or no question. You forfeit the rest of the game. Of course, I expected as much. And, as I might point out, that's a perfect example of why we've made our decision. Picard shot him a questioning look. Your decision. Yes, Captain. The verdict has been decided. You're guilty! Picard took a half step toward his adversary. Guilty of what? Q looked at him with unconcealed contempt. Of being inferior, of course. Seven years ago, I said we'd be watching you. And we have been. We've been watching and hoping that your ape-like race would demonstrate some modicum of growth. Give us some indication that your minds have the capacity for further expansion. Q's floating cushioned lowered so that his eyes were on a level with the captains. There was a hard-edged disdain in them that Picard had never seen there before. And what have we seen instead? You spent your time worrying about Commander Riker's career, listening to Councillor Troy's pedantic psycho-babble, helping wharf determine if he's a man or a mouse, and indulging data in his witless exploration of humanity. Picard stood his ground. We have journeyed to countless new worlds. We have made contact with new species, expanded the Federation's understanding of the universe. Q dismissed his comment with a wave of his hand. In your own paltry, limited way, but you have no idea how far you still have to go. Instead of using the past seven years to change and grow, you have squandered them. Time in the universe may be eternal, Captain. However, the patience of our continuum is not, and you and your kind have exhausted it. It sounded to Picard as if this was a battle he couldn't hope to win. It seemed that Q had already made his decision. And having rendered a verdict, Q, have you decided upon a sentence? Indeed. You see, it's time to end your trek through the stars, Jean-Luc. It's time for you to make room for other more worthy species. Picard didn't quite understand. You mean we're to be denied travel through space. Q's eyes flashed fire. No, you obtuse peace of flotsam! You are to be denied existence. Humanity's fate has been sealed. You will be completely and irrevocably destroyed! Picard was stunned. How could that be? Even a spiteful entity like Q was not capable of such an act. Q responded, having intruded into Picard's mind. There you go again. Blaming me for everything. Well, this time I'm not your enemy. I'm not the one who causes the annihilation of mankind. You are. You're doing it right now. You've already done it, and you will do it yet again in the future. The captain felt his teeth great together. What sort of meaningless double talk is that? Oh, my. He doesn't understand. I have only myself to blame. I suppose I believed in him. Thought he had some tiny spark of potential, but apparently I was wrong about him. Celeve! Picard sensed that the entity was about to make his exit. No, Q, you can't just leave it at that. Q didn't even seem to hear him. Good luck, Jean-Luc. Maybe you can still avoid killing every humanoid in the galaxy, but I doubt it. Hey, whatever God you believe in, have mercy on your soul, this court stands adjourned. As Picard shouted to get Q's attention, Q had already raised his hand, signaling an end to his audience. Picard sat up, fully awake. It wasn't until the sound had faded away to nothing that he realized he was in his ready room. And it took a moment longer than that for him to remember that he was in the present. Bolting to his feet, he made his way to the door and merged onto the bridge. Seeing that Riker wasn't there, he looked up to the intercom grid. Commander Riker, assemble the senior staff, go to Red Alert. We have a bigger problem on our hands than we thought. Thank you. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
description: In this episode titled "All Good Things - Side 2", Captain Picard and his crew discover the Enterprise is being targeted by other starships moving toward the neutral zone between Romulan and Federation space. The security chief, Worf, quickly activates a security alert while Picard addresses Miles O'Brien about receiving an alert regarding a large spatial anomaly in the Devron system. It becomes clear that the aliens aboard are not human, hinting at a sinister plot involving both Romulans and Klingons.

I should take my own advice and use them to relax Worf thought about his holodeck calisthenics program Most times I use them for other things besides relaxing As the Turbuliff doors opened depositing them on deck eight they stepped out The entrance to her quarters was just opposite the lift Next time Worf I'll choose the program If you like the black sea You're going to love Lake Kataria on betas end For a moment as they stood outside her suite Their eyes met and Worf basked in her scent He felt his discomfort slip away Deanna perhaps Before there is a next time We should discuss commander Riker She grinned playfully Why will he be coming along? No, but I do not wish to I mean it would be unfortunate if I I Do not want to hurt his feelings Deanna took his hand and hers Worf I think it's all right to concentrate on our feelings Yours and mine Her smile was contagious Gazing into her eyes reassured He began to forget about commander Riker as he leaned over to kiss her She lifted her lips to his But before they could touch the Turbuliff doors opened and the captain burst out of him Worf stared in disbelief not only was Picard uncharacteristically wide-eyed with panic He was wearing nothing but a blue and white striped bathrobe The card ran over to Deanna Counselor what's today's date the date? Star date 4 7 9 8 8 the card turned away from them and molded over Deanna looked at him Sir, what's wrong? The cards brow furrowed I'm not sure I don't know how or why but I believe I'm moving back and forth through time I I I In her quarters Deanna sat on one side of the smooth dark coffee table and Picard sat on the other side He was staring into the wispy vapors coming up from his tea And wondering why he couldn't get a better handle on what had happened It seemed to be on the brink of his consciousness teasing him, but when he reached for it, it slipped away He was simply too distracted to think much about drinking anything. It too much else on his mind Counselor it was as though I had physically left the ship and gone to another time and place I was in the past Can you describe where you were what it looked like? The captain sighed at the scent of the tea teased his nostrils It's also difficult to nail down, but it was years ago before I took command of the Enterprise. I Was talking with someone. I don't remember who it was dark outside then everything changed I wasn't in the past any longer. I was an old man in the future. I was doing something Something outside He cursed softly and bowed his head Sorry, I just can't remember It's all right captain. Have you considered the possibility that this was just a dream? No, it was more than to dream the smells and the sounds the way things felt to the touch They escaped me now, but at the time it was all very real How long did you stay in each of these time periods? Did it seem like minutes hours? I'm not sure at first There was a moment of confusion of disorientation But that passed and then I felt perfectly natural as though I belonged in that time I know this doesn't make much sense. It's a set of feelings more than distant memory Sensing that he'd run up against the wall the card focused again on his tea Vapers were no longer rising obviously he had let it sit too long Diana noticed as well. She reached across the table. Let me have your cup. I'll get you some more The card picked up the smooth ceramic cup and its matching saucer. He offered them to her He felt dizzy His hands reached out and took hold of the rough-skinned grapevine Suddenly the card had the strangest feeling that he had been about to do something else for a moment He felt lost out of place Peering out from under the brim of his straw hat He took in the long graceful contours of his family vineyard He saw the fog lifting off them in the low rays of the rising sun Still for just a second there it seemed to him. He was in another place altogether. Oh What the hell when people aged their minds were allowed to wander at them Captain Picard to the bridge Picard could scarcely believe his ears He looked up from his work and squinted as he shaded his eyes. He made out of familiar and welcomed visit Jordy Jordy La Forge His former chief engineer smiled with genuine enthusiasm as he approached Sir, I think we have a problem with the warp core or the phase endooses or some other damn thing Overcoming the stiffness in his knees Picard stood up Damn It's really you Jordy, isn't it? La Forge was wearing civilian clothes. He had left Starfleet a good many years ago Also, his visor was gone replaced by artificial eyes and his face was rounded by age Punctuated with a gray mustache He was no longer the bushy-tailed young officer that the captain had known La Forge held out his hand Picard grasped it with all the strength he could muster Good Lord Jordy How long has it been? Oh About nine years No, no, I mean since you called me Captain last When was the last time we were all together? only enterprise Close to 25 years Picard shook his head in amazement and smiled 25 years Time's been good to you commander The younger man patted his middle. It's been a little too good to me in some places La Forge took a look around his gaze finally fixing itself on the gardening tools that Picard had lugged out to the vineyard Can I give you a hand sir? The older man shrugged. Oh I'm just tying some vines I can handle it on my own The Forge knelt down anyway and examined one of the vines Looks like you've got leaf miners You might want to use a spray on them The card looked surprised to his knowledge the Forge had never set foot in the ship's botanical garden Much less acquainted himself with Terran parasites Commander what do you know about leaf miners? My wife is quite a gardener. I've picked up a little bit of it I mean just the other day she spent hours planting a single flower Without asking permission La Forge picked up a small length of shielded wire off the ground began tying some of the vines Picard knelt down beside him How is Leia? Busier than anyone has a right to be Even when she's not planting flowers The card stopped working and looked at La Forge So what brings you here? La Forge kept his eyes focused on the vines. He was tying. Oh, I just thought I'd drop by You know how it is I'd been thinking about the old days and the Enterprise and anyway, I was in the neighborhood Don't give me that you don't make the trip from Regal 3 to Earth just drop by You've heard haven't you? Well, Leia has a few friends at Starfleet Medical, you know, and word has a way of getting around I'm not an invalid, you know Erematic syndrome can take years to run its course I know captain, but when I heard I just I wanted to come by all the same The older man looked at his friend for a moment La Forge hadn't meant to offend him just to lend him support Well, as long as you're here You can help me carry in some of these tools La Forge grinned It's a deal Grabbing an armful of his farming implements, Picard saw his visitor do the same Together they started walking toward the house where Picard had been raised It was barely visible around the bend of the hill Suddenly the card stopped dead in his tracks Standing in the vineyards not 50 meters away was a trio of the saureas Scragliest excuses for human beings that he'd ever seen He didn't recognize any of them, so what in blazes were they doing in his vineyard? Before he could ask them that question They began pointing at him, pointing and jeering It was as if they found something amusing about him Out of the corner of his eye Picard could see Jordy looking at him with concern Captain, are you all right? Picard kept his eyes on the intruders I'm fine I just want to know what these people are doing in my vineyard Suddenly he felt lightheaded and slumped forward Captain? Are you all right sir? Picard turned at the sound of the shuttle pilot's voice He wasn't sure what had happened He seemed to have drifted off It was almost as if he'd been somewhere else until just this second somewhere very different from the shuttlecraft Galileo Perhaps he was just nervous he told himself After all it had been several years since he'd sat in the center seat of a starship Picard looked at the shuttle pilot Noting the way her prickly no nonsense attitude clashed with her strikingly good looks He smiled a little embarrassed I'm sorry Lieutenant yah My mind seems to have wandered for a moment What was it you were saying? I was asking if you'd ever been aboard a galaxy class starship before sir Picard focused his mind on answering the question No, I'm of course very familiar with the blueprints and specifications But this will be my first time aboard the young woman smiled Well then sir if I may be so bold you're in for a treat the enterprise is quite a ship I'm sure she is Lieutenant Picard found something about Lieutenant yah's face that seemed familiar He was relatively certain he had never met her before today Or had he? After a moment yah seemed to notice that he was scrutinizing her she glanced back at him Sir have I done something wrong? No, of course not, Lieutenant You just seem familiar to me I was wondering if we had run into one another on a prior occasion The woman's brow wrinkled I don't think so Enterprise to shuttlecraft Galileo You are cleared for arrival in shuttle bay 2 Working her controls for a moment yah are pointed to a spot dead ahead between two smaller starships There she is sir A moment later Picard saw what she was talking about as the galaxy class enterprise swam into view He felt his heart skip as he took in the majesty and the grace and the magnitude of her Her saucer section alone could accommodate more than a thousand people Her nacelles positioned underneath the ship where the star gazors had been placed above were not only elegant but highly efficient Even in the midst of all the other half-ready vessels in the yard She seemed to stand out to shine She's beautiful, Lieutenant Absolutely breath taken Captain Picard was in Deanna's quarters again holding out his ceramic cup full of cold tea His eyes kept going in and out of focus Tasha I was just with Tasha in the shuttle Suddenly it was all too much for him His accumulated feelings of disorientation swept over him like a tidal wave Somewhere off in the distance he heard the sound of his cup shattering on the table And he blacked out altogether Dr. Beverly Crusher had seen her friend to the captain in many a narrow strait However, she had never seen him look quite so meek or helpless as he did now Sitting in his robe on the biobed in front of her Jean-Luc was just staring into space and had been for nearly a minute He seemed oblivious to the doctors and nurses going about their business elsewhere in sick bay It made her feel helpless too Because even after the battery of brain activity tests she put him through she still couldn't figure out what was wrong Sighing she completed one last scan with her tricorder. I'll consider the results Troy who was standing at the foot of the bed looked at the doctor hopefully Unfortunately, Crusher would have to dash that hope I don't see anything that might cause hallucinations or a psychogenic reaction Troy turned to her Is there any indication of temporal displacement anything that might shed some light on the problem? Crusher shook her head Not that I can see Usually a temporal shift would leave some sort of tripamine residue in the cerebral cortex, but the scans didn't find any Gently she put her hand on Picard's shoulder He half smiled at the gesture, but his mind was clearly on his troubles But frankly Jean-Luc, I think you just enjoy waking everyone up in the middle of the night Picard looked at her grateful for her effort to ease the considerable tension Actually, I enjoy running around the ship in my bare feet. I find it invigorating Now it was the doctors turned to smile From the other side of sick bay crushers pregnant assistant nurse Alyssa Ogawa headed their way with a pad Here are the biospectoral test results Dr. Crusher Crusher looked over the results displayed on the pad Satisfied that there could be no error. She turned to the captain Well, your blood gas analysis is consistent with someone who's been breathing the ship's air for weeks If you'd been somewhere else There would be some indication of a change in your dissolved oxygen levels, but there isn't any such indication You haven't left the Enterprise on Luke Not as far as I can tell He frowned I don't understand Crusher turned to Troy Counselor would you be good enough to excuse us for a moment? Of course and captain I'll look in on you a little later Picard nodded But his gaze was fixed on Crusher Jean-Luc Our scans didn't show any evidence of aromatic syndrome But they did reveal a particular kind of defect in your parietal lobe The kind of defect that could make you susceptible to several neurological disorders later in life Including Eromatic syndrome Picard assessed the news Until that moment He'd only been dealing with something he'd experienced elsewhere Like in a particularly vivid nightmare Now the nightmare where at least this one aspect of it was invading his real world Crusher continued It's possible you could have that defect for the rest of your life without developing a problem And even if the syndrome does develop Many people lead perfectly normal lives for a long time after its onset Then why doctor Do you look like you've just signed my death sentence He said it with a hint of a smile so she wouldn't get the wrong idea But she was unable to quite bring herself to smile with him Sorry, I guess this has caught me off guard She wanted to say more But she was interrupted by the entrance of first officer Will Riker Crossing sick bay and several long strides He looked as serious as Crusher felt He held his hands out in a gesture of apology Sir Wharf's security scans have come up negative We're checking the sensor logs There's still no indication that you left the ship Picard slipped off the biobed It wasn't a dream number one Something did happen Wharf decapped at Picard There is an incoming transmission from Admiral Nakamura It is a priority one message Picard turned to Crusher Doctor may I use your office? She gestured for him to go ahead Entering the doctor's office Picard sat down at her desk and activated the desktop monitor After a moment the solemn visage of Admiral Nakamura appeared on the screen Captain I'm initiating a fleet wide yellow alert Starfleet intelligence has picked up some disturbing reports from the Romulan Empire It appears that they're mobilizing for something At least 30 warbirds have been pulled from other assignments and are heading for the neutral zone Admiral is there any indication why they would make such a blatantly aggressive move Our operatives on Romulus have indicated that something is happening in the neutral zone specifically in the Devran system Our own long-range scans have picked up some kind of spatial anomaly in the area But we can't tell what it is or why the Romulans might have taken an interest in it I see And what are our orders? As you can imagine this is a delicate situation I'm deploying 15 starships along our side of the neutral zone And I want you to go there as well to see if you can find out what's going on in the Devran system Am I authorized to enter the zone Not yet wait and see what the Romulans do You can conduct long-range scans send probes if you wish but don't cross the border unless they cross it first understood Admiral And with that the admiral's image vanished replaced with the official insignia of Starfleet Turning off the monitor the captain stood and felt a sudden wave of vertigo wash over him The card felt himself falling Reaching out until he was caught by a pair of strong arms Looking up he saw that it was LaForge who had rescued him Captain what's wrong With his friends help Picard steadied himself and looked around His family's vineyard seemed to stretch out forever in every direction But he didn't belong in the vineyard he tried to think I don't know what's wrong, Geordi I I wasn't here a moment ago But sir, you've been right here with me Picard groped for an answer he tried to concentrate to remember That the damned the rheumatic syndrome kept dragging down his every effort I wasn't there I was somewhere else, someone time ago I was talking to Beverly Beverly was there He looked up at LaForge and saw an expression of disbelief LaForge took hold of his arm It's okay Captain everything's going to be all right Flushed with anger Picard pulled his arm away I am not senile Geordi it happened I tell you I was here with you And then I was in another place it was It was back on the Enterprise At least I think it was the Enterprise it seemed like sick bay yes But maybe it was a hospital Picard shrugged how could he know how could he be sure LaForge looked at him with concern Captain I think we should go back to the house we could call a doctor The card felt his anger crawl up into his throat where it threatened to choke him No, I know what you're thinking It's the aromatic syndrome it's beginning to affect the captain's mind Well, it's not that and I wasn't daydreaming either dammit All right, sir. So something happened You've gone Somewhere else and back again Damn right I have Then what do you want to do about it? Picard considered the request and finally an answer came to mind I want to see data Because I think he can help If you don't mind my asking sir help how I don't know Geordi. I don't know but I want to see him Do you understand me? In the aftermath of the captain's outburst LaForge hesitated but in the end He seemed to come to terms with the idea Okay, sir. We'll go see data if that's what you want. He's still at Cambridge isn't he? Yes, I think he is Picard lost his train of thought Distracted by a sudden movement in the corner of his eye He saw the intruders again the scraggly undernourished hollow-eyed souls he'd noticed before But this time there weren't three of them There was six As before they were jeering and pointing at him He grabbed LaForge by the arm and with an effort managed to turn him in the intruders direction Do you see them? The forge looked out over the rolling vineyards See who? Picard pointed to them They're out there laughing at me. Why are they laughing damn it? LaForge put his arm around the card Come on captain. Let's go see data Picard started to protest But feeling a little weak in the knees He allowed his former comrade to guide him as they walked back towards the house When the card in LaForge arrived in Cambridge, they found that the university hadn't changed much over the several hundred years since it was founded Data's residence at the university was an old English manor house built around the end of the 16th century It had the smell of old wood about it As LaForge approached the front door with a captain at his side He noticed the large brass knocker molded in the shape of the long main alliance Reaching for the knocker, LaForge banged it a couple of times on the heavy wooden door After a moment the door opened A dower looking red-faced woman somewhere in her 50s and peered out of them Stated business My name is Jordy LaForge and this is Captain Jean-Luc Picard We're here to see Mr. Data were old friends of his The woman's eyes narrowed in annoyance I'm sure you are sir Everyone's friends with Mr. Data it appeared but the professor's busy right now and he can't be disturbed you see And she began to close the door Picard put his foot in the way It's very important we see him immediately We've come all the way from France The woman's expression indicated that she was not impressed Have you got wax in your ears? Now don't make me call the constable on you because I won't hesitate it Jessal, who's at the door? Jessal friend of yours sir I told him to come back another time Now Jessal I told you about frightening people away An inner door swung open revealing none other than their old colleague Data Being an android he hadn't aged over the years However, it was a prominent streak of gray on one side of his head Not a natural streak but one that looked as if he had taken a paintbrush to his head He was wearing a cranberry colored synthetic silk smoking jacket The perfect compliment to his surroundings Slowly a smile broke out on his face Jordy Jordy Captain it's been too long He held out a hand to them and turned to his housekeeper Jessal these are my old shipmates the ones I've told you about She was unimpressed All the enterprise bunched how delightful Turning on her heel she vanished into the house Unperturbed Data ushered them in What a pleasant surprise this is Tea and biscuits for everyone Jessal Data led them into his library which looked like something out of a Sherlock Holmes story Spacious, comfortable, the walls lined with a wide assortment of leather bound books The card could smell the oils that had been used to preserve them An authentic looking holographic fire was roaring cheerfully in the hearth There were any number of cats wandering about or sleeping on the furniture Data's experience with Spot hadn't turned him off to felines altogether Leforage nodded appreciatively This is quite a house you have here data. I see they treat professors pretty well at Cambridge and data shrugged Holding the location chair does have its perquisites This house originally belonged to Sir Isaac Newton when he held the position It has since become the traditional residence Just then Jessal entered the room with a silver tea service Wiping her hands on her apron she leaned in close to Leforage and spoke quietly As his friend see if he could get him to take that grey streak out of his hair He looks like a bloomin skunky does People will soon start walking on the other side of the street when they see him coming Data obviously overheard Thank you Jessal that will be all Without another word she made her exit Data turned to his guests with a rye look on his face She can be trying at times but she does make me laugh now and then Leforage smiled So what is it with your hair anyway? Data looked a bit embarrassed I have found that a touch of grey adds an air of distinction Unfortunately, I don't seem to have it quite right yet Crossing to the tea set he began to pour When he was done he brought them their cups Then sitting down with him he eyed Picard Since neither of you has a predilection for sudden visits I assume you are not here just for afternoon tea Picard nodded grateful for the chance to explain That's true Data I need your help It took a while for Picard to explain what had happened to him Even longer than it should have perhaps because of his illness But in the end he managed to get it all out I know how it sounds Data but it happened It was real I was back on the enterprise He saw Data and Leforage exchange a skeptical look Then as a dark brown cat climbed into Data's lap Data turned to Leforage When this happened Geordie did you notice anything unusual No data we were walking through the vineyard and he just stumbled Data looked back at Picard And you say this happened to you twice Twice that I know of Though I suppose it could have been more often Captain when was the last time you saw a physician about your aromatic syndrome Picard felt his spine has stiffened A week ago I was prescribed a pepidoxin and yes, I'm fully aware that it's not a cure Nothing can stop the deterioration of my My synaptic pathways I know that Again Data and Leforage exchange looks This time it rangled Picard You think I'm senile that this is all some delusion or something admit it Data gave him the unvarnished truth In all honesty captain It's a thought that has occurred to me However, there is nothing to disprove what you are saying either So I suppose it's possible that something is happening to you Picard felt hopeful as he watched Data pace across the room sending a number of sleeping cats scurrying for cover The first thing we should do captain is give you a complete series of neurographic scans I'll ask Professor Ripper to take over my lecture for tomorrow and possibly for the rest of the week Picard grinned That's my data. I knew I could count on you He jumped up from his chair and for a moment he felt like he was falling Picard felt his feet strike the unyielding metal of the shuttle deck Looking around he had that feeling again That he had been somewhere else until this very second A moment later he saw that there were a couple of dozen officers lined up for his inspection Stepping out from behind Picard Lieutenant Yarr called out in a loud voice the commanding officer of the Enterprise Shrugging off the last shreds of his disorientation the card moved to a nearby podium Placed his computer pad on it and surveyed the crowd Right now everyone was waiting for him to officially announce his assumption of command Moving forward with ceremony he was about to read from the pad when something caught his eye and made him look up To his astonishment there was a trio of humans up on the shuttle bays catwalk They were haggard sunken cheeked dressed in rags He had the strangest feeling that he had seen them somewhere before Though he couldn't remember where As he stared at them and they stared back One of the figures pointed to him then all three began to laugh The captain blinked unable to believe the evidence of his own eyes And they were gone Jarred he just stood there for a moment trying to decide what had just happened if anything Someone cleared his or her throat Remembering the officers who had assembled to greet him the card looked at them They were waiting Gathering himself he returned to the orders written on the pad You are hereby requested and required to take command A second time something caught his eye Lansing up He saw that the figures in the catwalk were back But now they were pointing at him and jeering even more wildly than before Then as if by magic They vanished again Unfortunately He couldn't puzzle it out now in the presence of all his officers They would think he'd gone over the edge Later after he'd had time to rest to mull it over He'd be able to put these things in some reasonable context Right now he wanted to get this ceremony over with and retire to his quarters After he read the words in the pad He stepped out from behind the podium And looked at his crew they looked back at him silently waiting for the first words he would offer them Before he could advise them He saw that the scraggly figures had returned and this time and force There were 10 of them now up in the catwalk all shouting at the card with murderous intent A fraction of a second later They were gone This wasn't his imagination Something was going on here And until he knew what he would take whatever precautions he deemed necessary He addressed his officers Red alert all hands to battle stations For a moment they just looked at him dumbfounded only lieutenant yard took it seriously right from the start You heard the captain move Their words broke them out of their initial paralysis An instant later they were sounding the alert rushing out the shuttle bay doors to their respective duty stations Later when Picard went to his quarters he found there was only a monitor and a couple of pieces of furniture in the anti-room Still it was a haven from the wandering glances of his crew who were no doubt still puzzled by his call to battle stations He couldn't imagine who would be calling on him, but he called for the person to enter As the doors opened they revealed a round of blue skined a bullion in civilian garb My name is Mott. I will be one of your barbers Picard stared at him There had been no barbers on the stargazer There simply hadn't been room for them Please to meet you Mott Please to meet you sir, of course I would rather be speaking to you as you sat in my barbers chair particularly as I can see that you're in need of some attention But like your quarters the barbershop is not yet fully equipped Picard nodded in what he hoped looked like sympathy I'm sure that problem would be rectified at the earliest opportunity the outfitting of your shop. I mean I hope so captain Picard You see a barbershop is a most essential facility on a vessel of this size Is a place where ideas are exchanged where consensus is are reached Where the social fabric is woven and rewoven I see what you mean as soon as we finished our visit I'll speak with the officer in charge of your deck and he or she will see to it that the barbershop becomes a top priority The bullion looked delighted How kind of you sir Then you will be invited to participate in the complete experience the bask in the glow of tradition of a well equipped shop I might have known you'd be a purist coming from a long line of vintners as you do Well, you'll be glad to know that barbering has been in my family for generations Almost as long as wine making has been in yours Something flashed through Picard's mind and he was no longer listening An image lingered dreamlike with a misty sunrise of a vine that needed tying And of a visit from an old friend with eyes that weren't quite right In the dream his hands were old and stiff and difficult to work with But his mind wasn't quite as sharp and his visitor was Jordy It came flooding into his brain a river and springtime overflowing its dam That vineyard existed in the future in his future Picard gasped as something else struck him The haggard figures he'd seen on the shuttle deck. He'd seen them in the vineyard as well Perhaps there had been fewer of them, but they'd been there just the same Pointing and deriding him as they had just a little while ago But why could only he see them? Who or what could be responsible? Then he knew Or at least he was able to guess Because his knowledge extended now over the 32 years that hadn't happened yet The bollion kept droning on until Picard interrupted Mr. Mott, I don't mean to be curt but there's a great deal for me to attend to Mott looked at him Oh, certainly I'll take my leave of you captain as you'll no doubt understand I have a great deal to attend to as well Picard couldn't imagine what that might be but he nodded knowingly and watched the bollion back out through the doors for the last parting way Picard was now convinced that he was shifting between three different time periods in his life He was just as convinced that he should not inform the crew of his experiences If it were true that he'd traveled to the past he did not want to risk giving them advanced knowledge of what was to come you
description: The podcast episode "All Good Things - Side 1" is an exclusive read by Jonathan Frakes in which Michael Jan Friedman narrates his thoughts on battle and music, focusing on the complex emotions of characters from Star Trek: The Next Generation. Despite their initial reluctance to interact with each other, these two individuals find themselves drawn into a romantic subplot that would significantly change their lives.

transcript: Simon & Schuster Audio presents Star Trek, the next generation. The Genesis Wave, book 3 by John Bornholt. Rent by Tim Russ. A red fog drifted across the two slivered moons of Torna 4, as she ran into the dingy alley. The disruptor beams streaked past her crouching body, charring the corrugated tin wall and burning a hole in the vacant building. She was the only one left of her species, and now they were trying to kill her. They wanted the bulky chrome box that she carried. She assumed them to be Romulans. It was so strange being known, being exposed, when she had operated for years under cover. She and the other seedlings had infiltrated every nook of the Federation to find out how the meat creatures could help them escape their dying world. With the Genesis technology, they had discovered a way to prepare new homes and propagate their species at the same time. All of that had ended three days ago when their world was invaded and their base destroyed. If the Romulans had tracked her down, it meant that they had ransacked the home base, deciphering the records. There was no other way for them to know that she had been entrusted with a portable Genesis device for a new experiment. She either had to destroy it or give it to someone who would do no harm. These could no longer benefit her species, but perhaps it could benefit someone. At that moment, the seedling salvation arrived in the form of a rowdy crew of bajaran miners and their consorts. The seedlings screamed out in her most helpless voice. Help! Please help me! The unruly party halted on the sidewalk and peered into the dark alley. The bajaran came stumbling down the alley and saw the pleasing bajaran shape she had become, at least to those within range of her spores. She absorbed their thoughts and knew she reminded one brawny miner of an instructor he had had in an orphanage. He took her arm and gingerly helped her sit up. What's wrong with you? They tried to rob me. The miner instantly ran down the thoroughfare, stomping and making his presence known. I don't see them. Let us ditch you some breast tuntie ale. That will fix you up. She touched the shiny metal box. Thank you. Don't forget my luggage. The miner dutifully picked it up. As they strode from the alley, the seedling glanced over her shoulder at the dark passage between the corrugated buildings. She hadn't bought herself more than a few minutes of respite, and her pursuers were probably already planning their next move. When they reached the tavern, most of the miners and their consorts went inside, but not the seedling and the miner carrying the box. She told him, what I want is someplace spiritual, like a temple or a chapel. You don't want to go there. They've been slammed with refugees from the Genesis wave. We've got to celebrate surviving the wave. An odd reaction thought the seedling, considering that billions of his fellow meat creatures had perished in the last few days, and billions more were homeless. But Torna Fore had been spared, and the sleepy backwater had turned into a bustling city hosting an impromptu festival. The seedling thought she saw someone in a black hood and suit moving among the convivial crowd. She tugged on the miner's shoulder. Let's go now. Phylar Yorka recoiled from the noise in the stench. His elegant, richly appointed bajoran temple had been turned into a warehouse for humanoid suffering. Yorka stroked the wispy gray hair atop his head. This was what he was trained to do. He had been where needed and helped the poor and afflicted. He pulled his maroon robes around his stout figure and tried to look officious. He was nothing more than a prylar, a monk, but this sect respected him as a former vetic in the assembly. Yorka was their leader in all but name and rank, and Yorka knew he had to lead his acolytes and volunteers through his tragedy. Yorka was besieged by Ferengi and he gritted his teeth. No one was more difficult to mollify than an impoverished Ferengi. A middle-aged businessman with three wives shook his fist with such anger that his earlobes wiggled. You've got to get us back to Ferenginar. I've got to file reports, insurance forms. I have no transportation to furnish, and you're free to leave or to stay in our house of worship. May I suggest that you pray to the prophets? We're having services in a half an hour. The Ferengi was incensed. It's not fair. I lost everything. Yorka raised an eyebrow. You still have your life and your wives. I recall two rules of acquisition, which I believe a Ferengi in your situation ought to consider deeply. The distraught merchant blinked at him with surprise, and even his wives drew closer to hear the words of the Bajoran religious figure. Rule number 236. You can't buy fate. And rule number 22.
