When you return my personnel, you may come along for a brief meeting and transmission. When Captain Picard stepped off the transporter platform, he spotted Commander Kalina standing in the corner, half bathed in shadows. She was taller than he expected, with a regal bearing. Her fierce eyes were darker and more intense in person. Welcome aboard the javelik, Captain. On behalf of my crew, thank you for your quick work in saving members of our boarding party. What action were you going to take next? He studied her carefully and decided to be truthful. We were going to send probes over. Kalina gave him a brief smile. We withdraw the request to search your ship, although you will turn over the prototype radiation suits made from our technology. And if we give you the radiation suits, you'll leave. She frowned. No, we have to investigate that derelict ship for our report. Picard nodded. We should cooperate and share information. If you will show me what you're doing, I'll try not to duplicate it with our probes. The elegant Romulan smiled again. Very well. I'll take you to our observation room and show you some of our scanner results. The observation room of the javelik was equivalent to the stellar cartography room on the Enterprise. It featured a brilliant three-dimensional display with multi-level platforms. Now the panoramic display had begun to shimmer and break apart. The mammoth warbird shook as if struck by a quantum torpedo. Captain Picard staggered to stay on his feet as did the Romulan commander. Commander Kalina to the bridge. Are we under attack? Are shields up? Pickle to Enterprise. He waited for an answer and none came. Pickle to bridge. A nervous technician looked up from his console. Commander Kalina, the patrask is no longer registering on scanners. Neither is the Starfleet ship. Picard whirled about. Which ship? The Romulan chef has read out. The derelict. The Barcelona. They were right next to each other. Another Romulan called out. Commander, there are ship-wide failures. Shields are down. Commander Kalina looked pointedly at Picard. The shuttle bay is not far from here. We could take a look for ourselves. Picard nodded and together they ran down the corridor. As a Ferengi businessman, Sherlock had been to some desolate commerce for mistaken places in his long life. But he had never been anywhere more foreboding than the moon of Meldra 1. The bleak wilderness had nothing but grey sand, weather beaten mountains and a few scrubby plants growing in the thin atmosphere. He had to draw frequently on the oxygen mask hanging at his side. He was glad it was Yorka carrying the box and not him. The Bajoran monk was followed by his two acolytes and their nervous shuttlecraft pilot, a young human female named Cassie Jackson. She spoke to Chelock. I thought you just wanted to see the usual spots, the usual tour? Chelock shook his head. This is where we want to be. Neither leave us alone or tag along and keep your mouth shut. With Yorka and the lead clutching his box, the small party trudged across the lunar landscape. The Bajoran was followed by the two acolytes, the pilot and the Ferengi who huffed liberally from his oxygen tank. Finally, Yorka set the metal box very carefully in the slate grey dirt. He knelt down in front of the box and reached for the delicate recessed handle. I'm going to open it. Chelock and the pilot Cassie Jackson drew closer, as did one of the acolytes. The other acolyte wandered up a craggy stone to take a look at something in the distance. Inside the box, a gorgeous red and black display glimmered in a language and symbols which Yorka had never seen before. Around this brilliant screen were large, jewel-like buttons, red, green, blue, plus yellow. You don't have a user's manual, do you? Yorka ignored the Ferengi and looked at his acolyte. Yellow is the color of the wormhole. Before they could stop him or say anything, he pressed the yellow button. The box seemed to be powering up. And without even thinking, Yorka pressed the green button with his thumb and the object began to vibrate under his hands. Praise be to the prophets! Chelock grabbed Yorka by the shoulder. Turn it off! You don't know what you're doing! Oh, I think I do, Chelock. In quick succession, Yorka hit the red and blue buttons. The back of the box opened, revealing a lens and a glowing beam shot out. Wherever it played, the land burst into flames, with brilliant green waves that scorched everything. Yorka realized that his youngest acolyte was somewhere out there in the midst of the searing green flames. He pulled the other acolyte back before he could step into the beam. Leave him! You can't save him! He's gone! As the green flames began to receive, shapes began to rise from the desolate moonscape. Enormous plants were growing at an accelerated pace. Yorka knew that this was a gift from the prophets. The beam suddenly stopped, and the small lens on the back of the box closed again. Prailar Yorka grinned with delight and threw his hands into the air. I have found it! The orb of life! The Ferengi gazed in awe at the incredible tangle of misshapen vines and sprawling trees. You know, I'm not really sure that's an orb. I have a better guess what it is. With a scowl, Yorka stepped toward the Ferengi. I say it's an orb. Okay, orb of life it is. Catchy name has a pre-soul recognition, and it delivers life. How do you want to promote it? I want everyone to know, especially the Vedic Assembly, but we also have to protect it. The pilot, Cassie, stepped into the conversation. Wait a minute. You need me more than anyone, because that mess of a jungle is going to draw attention. So what am I bid for one shuttlecraft ride out of here? Yorka jumped to his feet. You'll get nothing. You're just being an opportunist. Sherlock put his arm around the young woman. Ignore him. We'll give you all we've got as soon as we can. You don't bargain with somebody who has all the supply when you only have demand. With Commander Kailina at the controls and Captain Picard in the co-pilot seat, a small green shuttlecraft soared away from the space doors of the javelik. A vast field of debris floated in space where the Barcelona and the Patrask had been. A huge black curtain that blocked out half the stars was in their viewport. Without warning, a score of spinning tentacle creatures came hurtling through the confetti of debris, striking their shields. The craft shuddered, and Kailina announced. Shields failing. Something in the composition of those creatures. I'm shutting down everything but life support. They seem to be attracted to our energy sources. Without power, perhaps we can blend in with the debris. Captain Picard waited tensely as the Romulan commander worked the controls of the shuttlecraft. Suddenly, the instruments at every station went dark. It was almost peaceful, drifting among the sparkling remains of the two starships. They moved to the back of the shuttlecraft and began to put on environmental suits to protect themselves from any radiation. As the two of them stripped down, Picard couldn't help but notice that Commander Kailina was a fit, attractive female, with a statuesque frame to go with her regal bearing. When they had finally dawned the suits, they sat at the dark controls and gazed at the remains of the two great starships. It was numbing to think how many Romulans had been lost aboard the Patrask. Kailina turned to look at Picard, and her ebony eyes blazed into his. We have to join forces, Captain. I've lost a warbird with all hands on board. I want to work closely with you on this, until I am relieved. He frowned back at her. Do you think there will be such serious repercussions? Oh yes, we failed in our mission. Suddenly they were nearly knocked out of their seats. The shuttlecraft spun around, colliding with other rubble. Through the window of the shuttlecraft, Picard could see a ship coming closer. The Enterprise has got us. Yes, a tractor beam. The star-shaped creatures had also seen the Enterprise enter the debris field, and they masked into a steady stream headed toward the intruder. But after a few minutes, the shuttlecraft was finally inside the protective bubble of the Enterprise's shields. The familiar voice of William Riker crackled over his comb badge. Bridge to Picard. Captain, are you all right? Yes, number one. We are. Then stand by to transport. On the bridge of the Sequoia, the tactical officer addressed the newly appointed captain, Alina Nachayev. Sir, there's a hail for you from Admiral Whitcliffe. I'll take it in private. Make ready for launch. Nachayev ducked into her private office. Up came the welcome visage of an old friend. Good morning, Alina. We've been dealing with some very strange anomalies since the Genesis Wave. Disappearing ships and crews, strange creatures, unidentified radiation poisoning, and we've got no explanations whatsoever. Have my orders changed, Admiral? Not at the moment, Alina. They desperately need... you on low-mar. I just wanted to give you a heads up that the sequoia may be uprooted and sent elsewhere on short notice. With Cliff out. Taking a deep bracing breath of air, Nechayev strode back onto the bridge. Her first officer, Commander Marben's, gave her a fishy look. Of course it was hard for the blue-skinned bensite not to look fishy with those pale eyes, scaly face and blue tentacles all around his mouth. Marben's had expected to become the first of his race to Captain a ship after the sequoia skipper retired. Nechayev crossed to the captain's chair, wondering if Marben's would ever accept the fact that this was not his ship anymore. Has Mission Specialist Tetska reported on board? Yes sir, all personnel are accounted for. Begin launch sequence. Take us out to warp distance at one-eighth impulse. The galaxy-class starship began to move away from space dock, leaving the repair facility in Earth's orbit for the twinkling vastness of space. At optimum distance, Nechayev gave the command to enter warp, and they began the longest leg of their journey to low-mar. In the Enterprise's observation lounge at a meeting of the senior officers, Captain Picard paced in frustration. He turned to data. So, the probes that we finally launched have been destroyed? Not destroyed, Captain, absorbed into the dark anomaly. Picard frowned. If it can expand without notice, it's a ticking time bomb. Does anybody have anything to add? Dr. Crusher spoke up. My patient from the Barcelona, Lieutenant Slevin, is doing well and has given us a report on his experiences. He couldn't tell us much that we don't already know, but he felt that his crewmates were somehow absorbed into the dark entity. When no one else spoke, the Picard dismissed them. A short time later, Alyssa Ogawa strolled down a corridor with Lieutenant Rainer Slevin at her side, and the big Antosian smiled and greeted everyone they passed. If he could be returned to his loved ones, Alyssa reasoned, then why couldn't her husband Andrew be returned to her and Susie? Have you got any family, Lieutenant Slevin? He nodded. I had my parents and lots of relatives on Antos 4, but no wife for children. We Antosians tend to marry late. And what about your family? You have the worried look of a mother who wants to report home. That drew a smile from Alyssa. Since we're just taking a stroll, would you mind if we stopped at home to see my daughter? Absolutely. I would love to meet your daughter. When Alyssa opened the door, Susie's voice rang out. Mommy. The dark-haired imp came running through the living room and tackled her mother around the waist. Rainer Slevin looked on, his handsome face beaming at the sight of the reunion. Susie, this is my friend, Lieutenant Slevin. He came from the other ship, the Barcelona. Please to meet you. Susie crossed to a shelf by the dining table where several family holographs were displayed. She pointed to her father. That's my daddy. He's helping people get through the Genesis wave. He's been gone a long time, but he's coming home soon. With dawning realization, Slevin looked at Ogawa, who lowered her head. When Susie was out of your shot, the Antosian turned to Alyssa. I'm sorry about your husband. What are his chances? Alyssa sighed and looked away. He is missing, and that's all we know. Soon the three of them ate lunch, making small talk about Rainer's homeworld and some of the more famous escapades of the Enterprise. Afterwards, Alyssa and Rainer walked Susie to her classroom. At the door, Rainer bent down and shook her hand. It was a pleasure meeting you, Susie. Keep up your faith, and you will soon see your father again. Skipping happily, Susie headed into her classroom, but Ogawa frowned at Rainer. You shouldn't offer her false hope. Until she has no hope, I don't think it's wrong to give her some. Ogawa sighed heavily. I'll admit, I'm not sure how to handle this. She's at a difficult age, not old enough to hear the truth yet, but too old to be fooled. Rainer slept and smiled. You're never too old to be fooled, if it can spare you heartache. Tesco surveyed the humanoids hanging from the ceiling in the underground chamber on Lomar. They were encased in transparent bags which expanded and contracted at the rate of normal breathing. Shining a light into the morass, the Vulcan could see vines and clumps of moss snaking everywhere among the dark rafters. There were scorch marks and burnt bodies among those in suspended animation. In the battle to eliminate the moss creatures, the Romulans had decimated much of the life support system, dooming those hanging in suspension. Her human escort was Franklin Oswald, a medical officer. He had come to Lomar days ago and looked benumbed by his experiences. To him, these now were slabs of beef waiting to be catalogued and distributed. He gazed upward at the disturbing sight. Some of these bodies are centuries old, and so are the ships that were recovered. They must have needed them all to build this facility, but after that they stored them, just keeping a few active. We're still trying various techniques to revive them, but the Romulans made such a mess of things that it's hopeless, in most cases. Where do you want to begin? Tesco nodded solemnly. Admiral Nechayev wants all of them liberated and interrogated as quickly as possible. Oswald shook his head. That's the problem. Each one of these saw slaves was infested by the moss creatures, and that parasitic relationship is the only thing keeping them alive. It takes time to remove the vines and tentacles without hastening their death. Tesco reached up and touched the dangling foot of the closest humanoid who appeared to be a Vulcan like herself. Since saving their lives is virtually impossible, the logical procedure would be to interrogate them first. Oswald blanched. A bit cold blooded, isn't it? The Vulcan cocked an eyebrow. The Romulans have seized everything of value from this facility. Get me a ladder. We must find out if the Genesis Wave is about to be unleashed again. The invitation, which Chellak had printed on re-departement like the ancient books of prophecy, had read. You have been chosen to receive the most important revelation to the Bajaran people since the discovery of the Wormhole. Please report to Shuttle Bay 42 in the ancient city of Tampasa, one hour before dawn on the first day of redemption. The invitation was signed. Protectors of the Orb of Life. Chellak, along with the shuttlecraft pilot Cassie Jackson, had then flown to pick up the invitees. Vedic Zane of the Vedic Assembly, General Mira of the Bajaran Military, and government minister Gattrick were now on board. As they sat in the shuttlecraft, Chellak peered out the window. We await one more passenger, but we won't wait long for him, because he may have difficulty getting here. He's a wanted criminal. His name is Bacchus. General Mira jumped to his feet and alarm. Bacchus, the Marquis leader? Chellak shrugged. Please look around you, General. Every segment of Bajaran society is represented on this craft. Except for one, the rebels, the criminals, the outcasts. And they're as big a part of Bajar as any of you. Bacchus is known and loved among these people, and we have to tell them about this discovery too. The General wagged his finger at the Ferengi. All I've got to say is, this had better be good. Chellak squirmed. Well, you know how these orbs are. Good or bad, they're never boring. Cassie interrupted. Someone's coming. The person was wearing a simple monk's robe and a hood which covered his face, making it impossible to identify him. Without a word, the new arrival stepped into the shuttlecraft. When the guest pushed back his hood to reveal his face, there were several gasps of surprise. It wasn't another Bajaran, but a distinguished looking Vulcan. Slung over his shoulder was a large knapsack made from the same crude material as his robe. From a pocket on the knapsack, he pulled an invitation and presented it to Chellak. I am here to represent Bacchus. May I be seated. Without another word, the mysterious Vulcan sat down. Chellak took a seat beside the Vulcan as Cassie asked permission from shuttle bay operations to take off. Five minutes later, the shuttlecraft lifted off the pad. The six passenger shuttlecraft shot into warp drive with the cream of Bajaran society on board, having no clue where they were headed. Such was the drawing power of the orbs of the prophets thought Chellak. Even a fake orb was better than none.
description: In this episode of Star Trek Audiobook: The Genesis Wave by John Bornholt, we follow Simon & Schuster Audio as a seedling from the Genesis Project runs into an unexpected group of miners who offer to help her in some way. Despite initial reluctance, she is taken to a tavern where miners and their companions gather to celebrate surviving the Genesis wave that has displaced billions of species. As they discuss the event, the seedling's perspective on survival shifts, leading to a poignant reflection on how even the most brutal experiences can lead to moments of unexpected kindness and connection.

transcript: After Nachayev and Teska stepped off the transporter pad onto the deck of the Enterprise, the Admiral was astounded to learn from Commander Riker that Captain Picard had gone to Solosos III. I salute the Captain's initiative, but he's not the one I would have risked on that mission. Nachayev quickly introduced Teska to Riker, then proceeded. Commander Riker, there is a civilian run about just a few hours behind us. I want them to dock immediately on your shuttle bay before the Romulans can get a hold of them. Riker nodded. Then as he led them out of the transporter room, he told them about the recent spacewalk near the rift. We think we're ready Admiral, to go even deeper into the rift, which Councillor Troy thinks is related to the Gemworld rift. Nachayev scowled as they near the turbo lift. Say all I want to know, Commander, is how are we going to get that Genesis box off the javelik? Soon the trio entered the observation lounge where the senior staff was meeting, including Jordy Leforte who had recovered from his ordeal on the spacewalk. The Admiral sat at the head of the table and folded her hands. Of great concern is the possibility that these expanding rits, deadly radiation and weird creatures have been exacerbated by the Genesis wave. Starfleet reports that they've gotten worse with every demonstration of the so-called orb of life. But the relationship between Genesis, the orb of life and these rits, must be proven one way or another before we risk everything to stop Yorka in the Demilitarized Zone. Your Captain isn't here to help us get the Genesis emitter away from the Romulans, one way or another. If we had it, we could test it and we could verify with our witnesses that the orb of life really is a Genesis device. But fortunately I have also had some dealings with Commander Kalina. How is her health? The Enterprise officers glanced at each other a bit confused. Riker broke the silence. Her health? Yes. Kalina is older than me, somewhat frail and walks with a limp from an old war wound she refuses to get fixed. Puzzled, Riker shook his head. Well, that's not the Commander Kalina we've seen. She's young, statue-esque, beautiful. I can show you a video log of an earlier conversation the Captain had with her. Soon they were all watching Commander Kalina's first conversation with Captain Picard. Admiral LaChia have soon had a big grin on her face. That is not Commander Kalina of the Javelik. Those tricky Romulans, they never cease to amaze me. The Forge interrupted. Why would they do that? The women seemed to figure it out, and both Crusher and Troy gazed knowingly at the Admiral. Beverly spoke up. The Captain was over there with her for six hours on one visit. Are you saying that Captain Picard was infatuated with this imposter? The Romulans do have several means to accomplish what they did. We can assume that he told them everything he knows. LaChia rose slowly to her feet, thinking aloud. Since we've figured this out, maybe we could even work a con to get Genesis from them. But to do this right, we would need someone to impersonate Picard, someone who wasn't infatuated with their beautiful Commander. Crusher overcame whatever doubt she had and spoke up. I know someone on board who could impersonate Captain Picard so well that they wouldn't know the difference. He's a patient, Rainer Slevin, the only survivor of the Barcelona. LaChia have headed for the door, issuing orders as she left. We're going to get that box from them, by Hook or by Crook. Commander Riker, you are the acting captain, even after Picard gets back. When the runabout gets here, let it slip on an open channel that Regimal is with them. With that, LaChia have led Dr. Crusher out the door. In Sickbay, LaChia have crossed her arms and stared expectantly at the slightly nervous Rainer Slevin. Then she turned to Beverly Crusher. Before I put much faith in a medical side effect, Dr. I've got to see it in action. Crusher reached into her desk drawer and pulled out a photo of Captain Picard, which she handed to the Antosian. He looked at the photo and smiled. Uh, can you turn away for a moment? Watching me do this is like, uh, it's like watching a person get dressed. You want to see the end result, not how I got there. LaChia have motioned to Crusher to turn around. Not long after, Slevin spoke to them in a voice that sounded like Captain Picard's. You can turn back. Before them stood Captain Picard in an oversized uniform with the wrong rank, but Captain Picard nevertheless. LaChia have studied him closely. This is excellent. And you can maintain this facade for how long? Indefinitely as far as I know. Practice hard with the doctor to get this impression down and we'll meet again later. With that, LaChia have marched out the door. From the co-pilot's seat on the runabout, Reginald studied the short-range scans of the rendezvous point where they would be coming out of warp in a few seconds. Hmmm, a DeDereadex-class warberg. It has a cloaking module I helped design. Chelock was gazing worriedly over Reginald's shoulder. I don't like the odds. We've got to lower shields to dock inside the Enterprise and so do they. Reginald nodded. It might be a good idea to transport the crew off the runabout as we come in, as long as the shields are down. Reginald moved to the transporter console and sat down. The pilot reported. The Romulans are hailing us, telling us to go away. The pilot glanced at his readouts and squirmed in his seat. The Zekoi is taking matters into their own hands. They're powering up phasers. Suddenly the small vessel was jolted and Reginald nearly fell out of his chair. Twisting, straining her thrusters, the runabout began to slip toward a massive Romulan warbird. There's a tractor beam on us. An expanding blue beam shot from the Sequoia and swept over the javelik, giving the Romulan vessel a severe blow. The runabout broke free and careened toward the Enterprise. The Romulans retaliated with the brace of quantum torpedoes. The Sequoia maneuvered to insert itself between the warbird and the Enterprise. As soon as the Sequoia was in place, she raked the javelik's shield with an array of multiple phaser beams and kept the Romulan ship at bay. Reginald announced in the runabout. Enterprise, shields are down. And now hours are down. The doors are opening. Brace yourselves. The Romulans unleashed a phaser attack of their own. The Sequoia's shields took the brunt of it. Sparks flew everywhere in the runabout's cabin. But somehow the quivering, quaking runabout held together long enough to spin like a wounded duck through the open shuttle bay doors. Chelock was still screaming when the craft finally came to a complete stop. He rushed to the pilot and kissed him on his partially balled head. Great job. Beautiful flying. Pop that hatch. They were met by a dark-skinned human with opaque devices over his eyes. Welcome to the Enterprise. I'm Chief Engineer, Jody LaForge. The admiral would like to see Reginald and Chelock on the bridge. And by the way, the Romulans are demanding that we turn Reginald over to them. As they walked to the exit of the shuttle bay, Reginald sighed. I'm always so popular with my own people. When the forge, Reginald and Chelock stepped off the turbo lift onto the crowded bridge of the Enterprise, a tight-lipped ball-headed human stood before the viewscreen, addressing his attractive counterpart on the javelik. I'm sorry to have displeased you, Commander Kalina. But there wasn't any reason for you to fire at the runabout. That vessel belongs to a peaceful trade commission for Romulus and was stolen by an infamous criminal named Reginald. We demand that you hand him over immediately. The captain looks shocked. He is here under the personal invitation of Admiral Achaia Vomisakoya. Please, Kalina, if you and I could get together and talk about this privately, a slight smile graced the beautiful commander's face. You may come over, Captain Picard. If you bring Reginald with you. The captain could barely contain his joy at this point. We also have a prisoner from your trade delegation. Kalina nodded curtly. Just yourself and the two prisoners. The transmission over, the captain heaved his shoulders in relief and smiled shyly. Reginald frowned at the engineer LaForge. I'm not sure I like being handed over so cavalierly to people who want to kill me. LaForge smiled. That's not really Commander Kalina. But it's okay, because that's not Captain Picard either. Then LaForge led Reginald and Chelock to the observation lounge, where they soon found themselves seated around a large conference table, flanked by a stunning view of the warbird javelik through the viewport. Admiral Achaia have hovered around Captain Picard as if he were a valuable work of art, which might be stolen at any second. She turned to Reginald and gave him a rise smile. Welcome, old friend. We have to get a suitcase-sized box off that vessel. Where do you think they would store something so valuable? The Commander's quarters. On that vessel, the Commander has an impressive vault with dampening fields so you can't transport anything out. Nechia have leaned forward, her palms resting on the table. They've just given us a window to get a team aboard. Three people. She looked with a smile from Reginald to Tesca and then at the fake Captain Picard. As soon as the three visitors from the Enterprise materialized in the transporter room of the javelik, Captain Picard dropped into a crouch and waved a detonator in the faces of numerous helmeted security officers. Beside him stood two Romulans, shackled, risked to ankle. On the chests of each groggy prisoner was a blinking red device and Picard pointed ominously at them. Those are shaped explosive charges and this is the detonator. Do what I say or I will destroy us all I swear. Picard looked in vain for a face in the stunned crowd. I don't see Keilina here. I'm here to this transporter room alone or I will kill them. This episode was especially galling for the real Commander Keilina who stood in the shadows at the back of the transporter room. She barked in order and was the first one out the door with the others dutifully following her. Once in the corridor, she stationed a number of centurines to keep watch on the transporter room, although she didn't know that Reginald had already slipped through the bulkhead and was listening to her every word. Upon the Alasian, when this is all over I will take Picard as my own. Then the diminutive officer pointed at two more helmeted centurions. Go double the guard on my quarters. Reginald quickly eased through the bulkhead and back into the transporter room. When the door suddenly slid open, the imposter Picard rose to his feet. The young Willowie Commander Keilina stepped into the transporter room and took a few steps toward the distraught figure of Picard waving his detonator. A hand descended from behind her, applying pressure to certain nerves. With a surprised blink, the stunning Alasian fell to the deck. After rendering her unconscious, Tesca quickly turned the actress over so that Rainer could get a good look at her. He was already stripping down to change into a Romulan Commander's uniform. Now I've got to play an Alasian female, playing a Romulan female whom I've never met. Turn away please. Reginald though unseen spoke up. I'm leaving. See you at the loot. After Reginald left with the Commander's quarters, Tesca dragged the unconscious Alasian to the transporter platform. Rainer, now a duplicate of the beautiful Commander, joined them. Although shields were up, making it impossible to beam on or off the javelik, there was nothing preventing them from beaming anywhere inside the ship. Just as the Romulans forced the transporter room door open, the intruders disappeared and arrived in a storage room on level four, the traditional deck for the officer's quarters. Fortunately thought Tesca, the Romulan transporters didn't store used coordinates due to secrecy concerns. Leaving the Alasian, Tesca and Rainer who still looked like the young Kalina strode into the corridor. It was easy to spot the Commander's quarters because of the extra guard standing about. They were supposed to receive a signal from Reginald if he had gotten the Genesis emitter, but so far it only looked like chaos in the corridor. Then they heard his voice next to them. Here, the Commander's vault has got a double vault inside of it, which is too small for me to enter. We've got to blast it. Rainer's Slevin had an idea. Bring me pictures of the real Commander Kalina from her quarters. We'll meet you in the storage room. A minute later the three of them were back in the storage room, and Reginald handed Rainer a collection of holographic photos. The Antosian studied the photos of the venerable Commander. Then he exploited his side effect. Soon, Reginald and Tesca faced a rather dumpy, older Romulan female who looked like the real Commander Kalina. They moved into the corridor and many in the crew stopped to salute Rainer, which was a good sign. They strode up to the guards of the Commander's quarters. Open the door. After one of the guards finally responded and opened the door, the fake Kalina gave them another order as she brushed past them. We have to defend engineering. All of you report to engineering. Do it. As the door slits shut behind them, Reginald rushed toward a nondescript curtain near the door to the lavatory. He yanked it aside, revealing a large rectangular panel, which looked innocuous until one realized it was several centimeters thick, and the only lock worked by thumbprint. Reginald took off the bomb he had been wearing as a ruse, only now it was to be used for real. With a pained expression, he placed the charge in Tesca's hand. Now I must go lower the Javelick's shields while you secure the device. If the Enterprise is alert, they will beam us back the moment they see the Javelick's shields go down. But how will I know when you've got the booty? Tesca looked at him as if it were obvious. You will feel the effects of the detonation. Reginald smiled. Right. See you back at the big E. A second later he was gone, and Tesca began to rig the charge on the outer wall of the vault. Do not move. Tesca turned to see a Romulan disruptor level at her head. Holding it was an elder commander, Kalina. Tesca was surrounded by twinkling transporter beams, with armored centurions materializing in every square meter of the elegant sleeping quarters. In her opulent quarters, Commander Kalina waved her disruptor at Tesca's head. Cesar, but don't kill her. Tesca fought hard against them. Suddenly they started to collapse all around her. She looked up to see Commander Kalina mowing them down with a disruptor. Tesca realized the commander was her comrade, Rainer Slevin, who apologized. When they started beaming in, I figured I'd better pretend like I was on their side. Working with a measure of urgency, Tesca finished attaching the bomb to the vault door. When they had put as much distance and obstacles between them and the vault as they could find, they hunkered down and Tesca pushed the button. Tesca leaped over the smoldering barrier and feverishly dug in the rubble. By the time Rainer joined her in the blast hole, he had reverted back to his normal appearance. They finally found a scorched and slightly dented box underneath. An explosion shook the door and the Romulan stormed the commander's quarters. Just as a red disruptor beams streaked through the quarters, Tesca felt the tingling of the transporter taking her and Rainer back to the Enterprise. When they arrived, Tesca looked in vain for Regimeol. Suddenly a disembodied hand tapped her on the shoulder. It's okay, I'm here. Tesca held up the prize in triumph. Regimeol's wavering lightness solidified into view, and he was grinning. Nice working with you. Let's bring a loot to the admiral. Five minutes later, as he stood on the bridge of the Enterprise, Regimeol was not smiling as he watched the magnificent Romulan Warbird javelick careening out of control. One of its nacelles was aflame. Tiny fires burned all over her glistening green hull, and it looked like acid eating away at the corpse of some fantastic bird. He looked at the chaiiv. Did you have to do this? We admiral bowed her head. I'm sorry. We asked them repeatedly to surrender, but they kept firing. Data looked up from his console. The javelick is going into the rift. The great warbird banked into the glittering swirl of debris, cutting through the shimmering waves. In a final surge, the sputtering starship soared into the emptiness of the anomaly, and it was snuffed like a candle wick. After a brief crackle of energy, all was dark and still again. At the same moment in the cabin of a much smaller spacecraft, Jean Luc Picard suddenly dropped to his knees, gasping for breath. He felt as if a knife had been plunged into his chest. He slumped forward, wheelying. She's dead. Kalina is dead. He still loved Kalina fiercely, in death as well as life, but he no longer felt beholden to prove his devotion to her. He had loved and now lost, and the burning had been replaced by sudden embers of grief. And Picard picked himself up off the deck, and he looked around at his young crew. One of them approached him. Captain, there's a message from the Enterprise. Picard nodded gravely. I know. The javelick has been destroyed. Picard tugged on the bottom of his tunic. So what is our ETA to Solosos III? Three hours, twenty-five minutes, sir. Keep looking out for Cardassian patrols. Alert me when we get close. I'll be in the sleeping compartment. I think I can sleep now. In the Enterprise's observation lounge, Commander Riker and Tesco watched as Admiral Machiaev paced in agitation. We have a little over a day left, and it would take a day to send another ship to Solosos III. Riker sighed. Well, the Enterprise is too damaged, but we should send someone to back the Captain up. We could speed up repairs on the runabout, but we haven't got anybody who can legally travel in the Demilitarized Zone. Tesco almost smiled. Incorrect. You have a Ferengi on board. Riker nodded. Ah, yes. I forgot about shellock. I'll get busy on that runabout. Machiaev to Leforge. We need that test as soon as possible to see if there's a connection between the rift and genesis. Leforge answered from engineering. Admiral, we think we can supply just enough power to trip the emitter, but lower the output. Machiaev made her decision. Test it, but do it within the hour. I'll notify Starfleet to have everyone pull back from the anomalies. With their small shuttlecraft parked behind them, and the Sequoia monitoring them from a safe distance, Jordy Leforge and Data trudged across the fine gray sand of a nameless asteroid in the Rix system. Data easily carried a portable Genesis device under one arm. The device's power system had been doctored for low output, but in case they needed it, they had a backup box in a shuttlecraft, a replicate with an unaltered power system. Finally, Data set the metal box down. This looks like an appropriate spot. Leforge shivered although it was a perfect temperature inside his environmental suit. We're going to have moss creatures hanging from the trees. Data looked up from where he was finishing the final preparations on the doctored Genesis emitter. Jordy, there was no report of moss creatures in the two instances where these small emitters were used before. I believe these devices were designed to create temporary habitat. Just turned a damn thing on, Data. The android began pushing the colored buttons in the sequence that Chellock had told them to use. Jordy flinched when the beams spread out. The fearful green fire burned, shooting licks of flame about waist high, but the right combination of elements didn't seem to be present. Fievo plants twisted from the dead soil and noxious clouds swirled fitfully over the sputtering Genesis effect. Data looked up at Leforge. I believe we could use nano capacitors to sabotage virtually every one of these devices in existence. Jordy gave a sly smile. Well now that we've made it safe to play with, we can try all kinds of things. What if we amplified the power into a burst and overloaded the boxes? Then we might get a reverse Genesis wave in which the device would try to genocise itself. It could end up pulling Genesis energy back through the rits. Data nodded his agreement. But first Jordy, let us see how this experiment turned out. Data to Sequoia. Come in Sequoia. There was no answer, and the android cocked his head. That is not a good sign, Jordy. He picked up the spent Genesis emitter and dashed back to the shuttlecraft. Leforge arrived two minutes behind him, panting heavily. He found the android in the pilot seat going over screen after screen of readouts. Jordy, the rift has grown so large that it swallowed the debris field. Let's get out of here, Data. Data glanced back at the unused Genesis device in the rear of the craft. We must return to the Sequoia and talk to Admiral Nechai about another experiment. Jordy gulped. What I suggested was only hypothetical. I really don't want to overload a Genesis box and send it into reverse. Me and my big mouth. The tether stretched two kilometers. At the far end was a shuttlecraft manned by Data, and at the leading end was Deanna Troy wearing a brahms radiation suit. She gripped the handles of her jet sled and cruised slowly toward the immense blackness. Before anyone attempted to heal the rifts with a reverse Genesis wave, Admiral Nechaiev had agreed that someone had to explore the other side. Their solution had to help both sides and cause no peripheral damage or the cure might be worse than the disease. Plus, they had to answer the question once and for all. Had an accident brought the two dimensions into such perilous contact, or had the incursion from the other side been an attack as first suspected. The counselor was chosen to perform the mission because of her empathetic link with the entity which had once ruled the other dimension. She was convinced that the entity was dead or at least withdrawn. All she sensed was fear, overwhelming fear. Then she heard Data's voice within her helmet. I'm ready Data, Troy out. In the final few meters, she could see strange ungodly shapes writhing in the darkness like eels and a fish barrel. It was as if they were scared to come across, yet scared to remain where they were. And Troy couldn't blame them. That side was permeated by horrendous radiation. On this side there was only cold, unfriendly space. Their panic was bad enough when they had come across into inhabitable places such as the Barcelona, but when they ventured into the vacuum of space, they died in absolute agony. But to remain behind in their dimension was certain death. They were dying by the billions and billions, all because humankind had been foolish enough to create the Genesis device and plague God. With a blink, she was among them in a startling landscape of billowing blue clouds and a pale pink sky. More black planets and a gleaming purple sun were aligned in the distance. This dimension teemed with bizarre life, all of it in some kind of frenzied activity, flitting between the black barrier of her dimension and a grim mass of corpses which littered the clouds. Troy had to remind herself that hundreds of these rifts existed along the path of a Genesis wave, and this was only one of the many places where their dimensions crossed. With a burst of activity, panicked creatures rammed her jet sled and fouled the thrusters, and they oozed around her like sharks and a feeding frenzy. Still she was unafraid because they weren't attacking. She sensed curiosity and a desperate need for help. She closed her eyes and tried to communicate telepathically. To her surprise, an answer came. We know you. You killed us. A terrible accident happened. We can stop it. We can reverse it. We are dead. Overcome by feelings of grief and remorse, Deanna Troy began to cry. It's not too late. And there was no answer. She composed herself and hailed the shuttle craft. Deanna, bring me back. You need to close this rift by any means available. We can't make matters worse than they already are. With relief and sadness, Troy felt herself being pulled back into the darkness, and the creatures squirming around her withdrew in fear. A moment later she floated in space on the edge of the abyss, and she began to cry again for all of those who had perished on both sides of the rift, killed by a machine which was supposed to create life. Wearing an environmental suit, Jean-Luc Picard stepped gingerly out of the Captain's yacht onto a foggy planet with crystallized dirt and swirling yellow clouds. An acid-filled sleet bombarded him. It was hard to believe that Solosos 3 had once been a thriving Class M planet with a happy colony of Federation citizens. All of that had been destroyed by the Federation itself, and now Solosos 3 was mired in a trilithium winter. It had taken them hours of searching from orbit, but finally they had spotted life signs, about 20 of them. Now time was running out, and Picard wasn't even sure what he was looking for. Picard spotted one of his young crewmen. They dared not use combages to talk to one another, so he walked stiffly toward his companion until they were helmet to helmet. The ensign held up a pad with text on it. The Captain took the handheld device and read it. With surprise he noted that it was from data. There were detailed instructions on exactly what he was supposed to do with the network of Genesis devices when he found them. He was to patch into the network, reverse the current, and overload it with as much power as he could muster. As the ensign stole away into the dense yellow fog, the Captain slipped the pad containing his instructions into his pocket. He took out his tricorder and attempted to locate the life signs they had spotted from orbit. Their quarry were less than 500 meters away. He took another step and nearly tripped over a fat electrical cable which looked new, and it led in the direction where the life signs were congregated. Following the cable for about 100 meters, he found one of the Genesis emitters, its instrument panel blinking ominously. He considered patching into the device right here, but that would no doubt alert Yorka and his party. He would either have to find some way to neutralize Yorka's crew, or he would have to wait until he were gone. Stalking in a crouch, Picard followed the cable until he spotted a shadow in the fog. He instantly threw himself to the ground and inched forward on his stomach to a spot where he could clearly see an armed guard wearing an environmental suit, festooned with the insignia of the pejorin. Picard drew his phaser. The guard dropped to the crusty dirt, and Picard threw his prisoner over his shoulder and carried him back to the yacht. Half an hour later, Picard was wearing the pejorin environmental suit as he again followed the electrical cable to its source. Ghostly buildings loomed ahead of him in the fog. As he drew closer, he noticed that one of the buildings had a protective tent stretched over it. A figure suddenly emerged from the mist, startling the captain. But when the figure saw Picard's pejorin suit, he waved in a friendly fashion. Picard waved back and continued on his way. In the middle of the street loomed another recognizable shape, a pejorin troop transport. There were probably people inside, but his destination was the tented building which he assumed was the headquarters of this misguided mission. A guard waved as he approached, and Picard again drew his phaser. After drilling the guard with a stun beam, the captain dragged the unconscious pejorin into a foggy side street, then he took his place at the door. After a short while, he slipped inside the airlock. He found himself in a church. He knew the air was breathable because several unsuited pejorins were hovering over a portable generator. Electrical cables snaked from the machine out every door and window, and the Genesis device blinked ominously in the corner. A heavy set bejorin paced in front of the altar, glancing frequently at his work crew. A young blonde woman lounged in the pew in the front row, calmly filing her nails. They had to be Vedic yorka and Cassie Jackson. Picard thought it was hard to believe that these blundering fools were about to shred the fragile curtain between dimensions, but possessing Genesis made them the most dangerous force in the galaxy. Vedic yorka sighed impatiently. What is taking so long? We've promised people. They're waiting for this moment. One of the technicians bowed. Excuse me, your holiness, but the stress tolerances have to be exact if we wish to activate all the emitter in unison. We're almost ready. Cassie Jackson rolled her eyes. Why don't you pray to the prophets for some patience? The rotund Vedic wagged his finger at her. Don't you take the name of the prophets in vain? You're only doing this for the money. I'm doing it for the greater good of all bejor. As they talked and the technicians worked, Picard maneuvered along the back wall hoping to make it down the side aisle and get closer to the generator. He drew his phaser out of his pocket and put it on a destructive setting. His intent was to take out the generator and worry later about data's instructions. Yorka suddenly spotted him. You there? Get back outside. Get back on guard duty. Picard turned to leave, but stumbled as he walked trying to stall for time. At the same moment, a suited figure charged through the airlock and raised his helmet. I'm not a quirk, you're going to be a good guy. We spotted a shuttle craft. Suddenly all eyes turned to look at Picard and the guard at the door rushed him, grabbing his phaser hand and forcing the weapon upward. The captain didn't mean to shoot, but he blasted a thick blue beam at the ceiling, a chunk of the ceiling disintegrated and plaster and debris rained down on them. Worse than that, the deadly yellow fog rushed into the room like a pale ghost and the bejoran who had been struggling with Picard gagged and went limp in Picard's arms. In a panic, his bejoran comrades rushed toward a pile of environmental suits, but none of them made it. Within a few seconds, everyone in the room but Picard lay on the floor, writhing in agony. Victims of the trilithium-tinged air. The captain instantly drew the pad from his pocket and rushed to the generator. He studied data's notes, then looked at the generator and the cable snaking away from it. Suddenly, three shimmering columns glowed in the center of the church. Before shooting, Picard waited a microsecond until he identified their environmental suits, which were Starfleet. He held up his hands. It's me, Picard. One of them strode toward him. Could you use a little help? Yes, guard the door. His order came just in time as the bejoran militia began their assault in earnest. Picard tried to clear his mind and concentrate on his task. He wouldn't have to patch into the network because the hub was right in front of him. Still, it seemed ludicrous to set off the string of Genesis devices when they had tried so hard to prevent them from being used. But data's instructions were explicit. The captain carefully reversed the charge and set the system to overload. He pushed the button. Smoke wafted from the glowing circuitry of the Genesis device. Picard held his breath, thinking they would all be blown to bits or mutated into primordial sludge. Instead, he began to feel enormously happy and relieved. A wave of tranquility swept over him and he wept with unbridled joy. The firing stopped and both sides dropped their weapons and stood perfectly still, gazing in awe at each other. Even the dying bejorans, who had been writhing in agony a second before, smiled blissfully at one another. Throughout the galaxy, in the depths of the oceans, in grimy caves, in palaces and prisons, the starships and star bases, every form of life from Melkoshans to Amoeba's experienced one shining moment of peace. All living things felt connected, part of a single, wonderful creation. What has happened? Picard turned to see Vedic Yorka crawling toward him, his eyes begging for understanding. He went to the bajaran, knelt down and put a hand to his feverish brow. You have done this, Vedic. With the orb of life you have brought peace to the universe. The joyous smile which graced the monk's face brought another round of tears to Picard's eyes. A second later, Vedic Yorka was dead. Picard looked up to see Cassie Jackson staring at him. He smiled as innocently as a child as life ebbed from her body. Without saying anything, the bajarans began to collect their dead. One of the Starfleet officers approached Picard and offered him a hand. When he stood up, the captain got a good look at his rescuer for the first time, and he was surprised to see it was a pharingi. Good thing you started blowing things up, or we never would have found you. Ready to go home? As Admiral Nachayev stood in the transporter room of the sequoia, she extended her hand to her former first officer, Commander Marbins. I speeded up the paperwork for you. This is now your ship. Energize when ready. A moment later she stood on the much smaller bridge of a runabout, facing the Romulan Regimal and the feisty pharingi shellok. Regimal gave Nachayev a broad smile. Our crew is complete. Where to Admiral? Our first stop is Pharinginar. We need to get our friend shellok home. Wait a minute. I risked my life, and this is the kind of thanks I get for saving the universe? Nachayev smiled. Shellok, by the time we get there, you will have the exclusive holodeck concession on our revamped starbase 411, which I understand is a very lucrative contract. Shellok fell to his knees and began kissing her hand. Oh, Admiral, thank you. Thank you. Are you single? Nachayev quickly withdrew her hand. That's enough of that. Captain Regimal, I think we can be going now. Aboard the Enterprise, Beverly Crusher sat near Captain Picard in his quarters, doing her best to make him feel better. Jean-Luc, prisoners have been released everywhere. It's a new dawn of peace and understanding. Even the Romulans have volunteered to destroy their Genesis emitters after what's happened. Picard shook his head in sadness. Truthfully, the pain of Keleena's death still hurts me, Beverly. No matter how or why I was in love with her, I really loved her. I would have killed for her. Betrayed Starfleet, whatever you can think of, I would have done it. In one way, I'm grateful, because I never knew I could love like that. Beverly smiled. I was more shocked before, but now I'm really jealous. He gave Beverly a tender squeeze and a sly smile. I'm still in a romantic mood, Doctor. Diana Troy sat in the saucer lounge of the Enterprise with Will Riker, gazing out the observation window at space. Just space. There was no blackness, no rift, no sea of sparkling debris, nothing but blessed beautiful space. Although Troy was relieved that the threat was over, in a way she was sad that the mysterious entity had again vanished into its own dimension. Twice now she had encountered the being while convinced it was the enemy, only to find out it was actually the victim. Some day she would like to renew their acquaintance under less adversarial conditions. A penny for your thoughts, Diana. I have many thoughts, Will. One of them is that I'm very happy to be here with you. There is, that it seems to be a natural tendency for us to want to play God. For all our meddling, we still don't know much. The problem is that we tend to learn through trial and error, and playing God isn't one of those places where error is easily forgiven. We were lucky this time. Diana took a sip of her hot chocolate while she gazed out the window, and another thought occurred to her. What is to become of the Brahms suit? Can we keep using them? We're in negotiations with the Romulans. They'd like to get Leia Brahms in custody and put her on trial for espionage, but we're not going to let that happen. No matter how much peace there is in the universe, some things never change. Riker took her hand. Diana, we're going to need you when we get to Bajor. We have a lot of ruffled feathers to smooth over and a lot of explaining to do. For example, they think Captain Picard killed one of their vedics. We may be there for weeks sorting this out, but you and I might be able to slip away for a little side trip to Deep Space Nine. As she held her beloved's hand, Diana Troi smiled. Will? I'd like that. From the planet Vulcan, two solitary figures stood on a foreboding mountaintop, overlooking an arid, copper-colored plane which was bubbling with lava pools. One of them was dressed in the regal scarlet and beige robes of a priestess, and the other wore a simple monks garment. It had taken the better part of a day to climb to this isolated place, but Tesca felt she had to make the trek. It was a place where she and Hasmik had come often to meditate and make love. The priestess took the hand of the Romulan beside her and motioned across the expanse of the rugged plane. Do you like it, Jarrett? It is called the Valley of Everlasting. Yes, I do like it. I'd always heard that Vulcan was an ugly planet, a barren wasteland. But this is beautiful. Tesca took a deep breath and continued. This valley is old, eroded, beaten down. Yet the lava replenishes, creates, and makes it new again. This is a place I came often with my mate. Jarrett hung his head and averted his eyes. He tried to pull his hand away, but Tesca squeezed it all the tighter. In our belief, Jarrett, the katra is our soul. The essence of our being. Just before death, a Vulcan uses the mind-meld to entrust his katra to a loyal friend so that he can share it with the departed's loved ones. I know that neither you nor Hasmik are Vulcan, and have no training in this. But yet when we melded, I sensed that Hasmik's death made a deep impression on you. It was not just a memory, but an event which represented much of what was wrong in your life. As the last person he saw, you undoubtedly made a strong impression on him. Because of this, I feel that Hasmik lives on in you. The Romulan looked pained, but I killed him. He's dead because of me. Tesca shook her head. No. That is like blaming the knife. Here you should blame me or my uncle who arranged our marriage. Or we could blame our feuding ancestors who tore the Vulcans and Romulans apart millennia ago. The past is like a pool of water. Put your hand in anywhere, and the ripples spread across the entire pool. It is all joined. There is no way to separate one event from the other. Now Jarrett gripped her hand and looked plaintively into her eyes. I want to make it up to you, Tesca. I want to make it up to everyone I've harmed. She nodded with understanding. Like this valley, we constantly reinvent ourselves. You, Jarrett, are not the same person who killed Hasmik, and I am not the same person who married him. We spent a great deal of time apart, which both of us saw as normal. In hindsight, I am uncertain of the wisdom of that. Being apart made both of us weaker. It doomed, Hasmik. Tears came to Jarrett's eyes. If you were mine, Tesca, I would never leave you. Tesca took Jarrett's hand in hers. You speak with the learned wisdom of all three of us. Now look into my eyes, and I will speak the ancient ritual of grief and loss. Only Hasmik is not lost. He has been found. Star Trek, the next generation. description: In "The Genesis Wave Book 3 Part 3," Captain Picard and his crew face a new threat on the space station Solosos III, following the events of their previous journey through the Gemworld rift. Commander Kalina's involvement in the mission adds an unexpected dimension to the plot, as she attempts to assist Starfleet but seems ill-prepared for her duties due to her age and health issues. The Admiral is concerned about the impact of the Genesis wave on the crew's safety, while Riker must navigate the complexities of their relationship with Commander Kalina and address the Romulans' plans to stop Yorka in the Demilitarized Zone. The episode explores the challenges faced by Captain Picard and his team as they attempt to protect themselves from dangerous radiation and weird creatures, all while trying to prove the connection between Genesis, the orb of life, and these rits.

transcript: In the underground chambers of Lomar, Tesca almost lost count how many mind-melds she attempted on the slaves hanging in suspended animation. Even restricting herself to those who seemed relatively healthy according to tricorder readings, it was an exercise in futility. She found brain activity, subconscious functions such as breathing and heartbeat, plus a few basic emotions. There were memory fragments, but they seemed false and removed from reality like half-remembered dreams. Her breakthrough came on the 22nd subject. It was a human female. As soon as Tesca inserted her hand into the slimy innards of the bag and touched the face of the blonde woman, she felt a slight shock. Tesca signaled to Oswald the medical officer with her. Then recording. Then she began relating their thoughts aloud. You are being held prisoner. Do not be alarmed. You are safe now. You are in suspended animation and our minds are melding. We need information to help you. My name is Tesca. Who are you? Tesca Linda Fini Linda. This is crucial. What is your job here? What project were you most recently working on? Engineer, second class. I am working on the portable emitter. The small one. The Genesys emitter? Yes. A small version for tests. Also for the backup plan. How many of these devices did you make? A few. I saw others working on them. And where are the portable devices? They are in the laboratory. One is in the field. Torna for. Can you save me? Tesca nodded. We will try, Linda. Vivulkin broke off the mind meld, letting Linda Fini drift back into her troubled slumber. Tesca stepped down the ladder to where Oswald waited. Oswald was troubled. But sir, we haven't found any portable devices like that. Tesca fixed her colleague with a baleful gaze. But we were not the first ones here. I must inform Admiral LaChayev immediately. After hearing the Vulcan's report, Admiral LaChayev frowned deeply and rose from the desk in her ready room. This coincides with another report I received. The large moon of Meldra 1 had sudden and inexplicable plant growth over 12,000 square meters of land. And we're talking about an arid wasteland. Nobody knows anything about it except that a shuttlecraft and a few passengers from a freighter are also missing. The admiral sat back at her desk and began working at her computer terminal. Engineer Fini said there was a device on a planet named Torna 4. The freighter which went to Meldra 1, it came from Torna 4. Tesca cocked an eyebrow. That is near Bajor if memory serves me. We must cease operations here and go to investigate. LaChayev looked up with alarm. We've got work to do here, lives to save. It is a logical assumption, Admiral, that unknown parties have a portable Genesis device and tested it on a moon. It is also a logical assumption that these unknown individuals obtain the shuttlecraft and have escaped, perhaps, to go into hiding. They are not Romulans. Romulans would not test the device in Federation's space where the results could so easily be identified. LaChayev groaned. No, I suppose not. You are married to a Romulan. Do you have any contacts there? Tesca shook her head. The whereabouts of my mate are unknown, and I trust no other Romulans. We must investigate this ourselves and do so immediately. LaChayev stared at her computer screen. The best I can do is report all of this to Starfleet and ask for guidance. You're dismissed. LaChayev looked up from her desk, scowling, but she had to admit the truth. Tesca was right, and it would shake the admiralty to their core when she told them that the Romulans had possession of Genesis. And there was nothing she could do about it, not while she orbited this dead planet, struggling to keep scores of brain dead patients alive. Piloted by Cassie Jackson, the small shuttle craft swooped downward into a landing approach. The five passengers looked at Chelock suspiciously, except for the Vulcan whose expression hadn't changed in several hours of warp speed flight. Two specks on the ground turned into two pejorans, a fat one and a thin one, who covered their eyes from the blowing sand as the shuttle craft settled to the ground. As the passengers stepped from the craft, a beaming pylar yorka greeted each one. Chelock and Cassie stepped out of the craft and leaned against it with their arms crossed. The Ferengi wanted to take over the presentation, but he knew this was Yorka's show. When it came down to asking for cash and support, he would perform that onerous task. To him, that was the important part of the ceremony. General Mira came to the point. All right, Yorka. You've got us here. Now what? The monk turned to his waiting acolyte. Fetch the orb. The dour bejoran acolyte nodded and hustled into a tent. A moment later, he emerged, holding the familiar metal box in his hands. With reverence, he handed it to Prylar yorka. Vedic Zane perused the gleaming box. That doesn't look like any arc I've ever seen. Minister Gattrix woke up. Do we look at it one at a time? Yorka shook his head. No, this isn't the kind of orb one gazes at in quiet contemplation. The orb of life is more of an active orb, as you will see. Yorka opened the container and pressed the buttons. When a blazing wall of green flame consumed the barren land, and the wind began to howl, while the sky darked with furious clouds, the observers clustered together nervously. Minister Gattrix screamed over the wind. This gives an abomination. The general shouted, no, we must have it. The Vulcan calmly pulled out a pad and began to take notes. With a satisfied grin on his face, Prylar yorka walked back to join his guests, and Chelok jumped into the conversation. Let's step into the shuttle craft, where we can talk terms away from all this noise. We have immediate needs for cash. The Vulcan reached into his bag and pulled out a thick ingot of gold pressed platinum, which he promptly handed to Chelok. There is more where that came from. The Ferengi smiled at the tall, noble Vulcan. I think I like you, best of all. Yorka motioned to Chelok to follow him away from the others. A private word with you, Chelok. I didn't have a chance to tell you, but while you were collecting our guests, we inspected the orb and found the power supply had weakened. The Ferengi blinked in surprise. Well, then, how did you make it work? That was the replicate we used. Chelok rubbed his hands together. That is good news, but we don't want every household on Bajor to have an orb of life. With a doubtful look on his face, the Prylar glanced at the teeming forest sprouting miraculously from Baron Sand only a few meters away. Monsterous black trees now towered in the sky. He tried to embrace her again, but she slipped out of his grasp and walked to the door. Don't come back to me, Jean-Luc, until you have it. As the door shut in his face, Picard knew what he had to do. The SACOIA TESCA entered the Sequoia's brig alone. She knelt down in front of Jarrett, the Romulan assassin. They had to be equals. Jarrett, are you ready to melt with me? After a few seconds he looked up and shrugged. Why not? Come on in, Vulcan priestess. But I warn you that my mind is not a pretty place. TESCA alighted on the bunk beside him and began to massage his neck until he began to relax. Do not be afraid, Jarrett. I am giving, not taking. As gently as she could, TESCA spread her delicate digits across his left cheekbone, forming a pattern of contacts. Almost immediately, the bloody images and raw sensations rushed into her mind. For a Romulan, Jarrett had not lived a life of privilege. He was born to poverty and low caste, the child of a comfort worker, as they were called. He was raised in a brutal orphanage. He showed a penchant for inflicting violence, and he was taken to a special school. Inflicting pain and death was Jarrett's art. In some respects his life flowed peacefully with a predictable outcome. Then a shred of Jetsam flew past, which TESCA had to pluck from the stream. In her hand, the bit became an ugly pool of memory, which she found to be deep and frigid. Yet TESCA dove in and swam to the center. Yes, she saw it all, including the one death she could not bear to watch. Hasnik, standing tall and defiant, professing his innocence while professing his love for his Vulcan mate. At that point, Jarrett wrapped a shroud over TESCA's eyes and spirited her past the actual scene of Hasnik's death. He died bravely, said the Romulan. The two of them merged and melded their thoughts, dreams and desires, becoming intimate in a way even lovers dared not. Jarrett's mind was ugly because it was deprived of beauty, and TESCA's mind was beautiful but deprived of wildness. At that moment, they awoke, tears welled in the hardened Romulan's eyes, and he gripped her forearm and wept on her shoulder. I... I killed your husband. I'm so sorry. TESCA patted him tenderly on the back. It was my good fortune that it was you, Jarrett, because now I know Hasnik is indeed dead. TESCA TESCA entered the ready room to find Alina Nachayev pacing. The admiral pointed to a screen that contained an urgent message from Regimal. Regimal and the Ferengi Cheluk had gone to rendezvous with Yorka and Cassi Jackson. They had found no one, But they had retrieved what Regimal described as an invitation. The admiral walked over to her screen and pressed a panel. Tesca, I want you to hear this part of Regimal's message. Regimal appeared on the screen and read from an ornate document. On the seventh day of circles, the light will conquer the dark. Good will triumph over evil. And the graveyard of our allies will blossom with life once again. Watch the heavens, for you will experience the wonder of the orb of life. Signed with humility, Vedic Yorka, protector of the orb of life. Regimal looked up with a slight smirk. His Vedic ship didn't waste much time getting his old job back. We have two days. When the transmission ended, the chai have sat down, speaking her thoughts aloud. Two days. We've got to stop Yorka from deploying Genesis on a large scale. That means solving the riddle of Yorka's announcement. At the same time, we've got to get our hands on a Genesis emitter to test it and see if it really affects the anomalies. We know that the javelik has an emitter, but how do we get it from them without destroying the warbird and the device? And without losing the sequoia and the enterprise in the process. Teska stepped forward. Admiral, we should bring Regimal back. To steal an object from a Romulan warbird, we need him. The Admiral nodded. Yes. We will inform the runabout to meet us at the Enterprise's position. I'll bring Captain Picard up to date. Teska, you research the clues in this message. Use as much of the ship's resources as you need. Captain Picard glared at the senior officers gathered in the observation lounge. Let's recap, shall we? The Romulans think we have a portable Genesis emitter and we don't. We think they have one, but maybe they don't either. And the only person who for certain has Genesis is this Bajaran monk, Yorka. Only he calls it the Orb of Life, and maybe he's going to replicate it. A daisy chain, a number of them, and presumably terraform a place called the graveyard of our allies, two days from now. LaForge lifted his dark eyebrows over his pale implants. If the Romulans find out about this mast detonation, they'll probably head right there. A slight smile played across Picard's face, presuming they can figure out where it is. LaForge continued. One thing is certain, we need a Genesis emitter to see whether its energy really affects the rifts and the radiation levels. Rikers sat forward. Perhaps we should schedule the EVA in the Brom suits before the Sequoia gets here. After that, we might be in action. Picard rose to his feet. There won't be an attack on the javelik. I...I can talk to her. Picard's a bridge. Hail the javelik for me. Sorry, Captain. The javelik continues to ignore our hails. Picard slammed his fist into his palm with frustration. I am not going to play this ridiculous game. Number one. Go ahead and schedule the EVA using the Brom suits. And I want a small crew assembled for the Captain's jot. Somewhere out there is a Genesis device, and I'm going to find it. With that, he marched out of the observation lounge without dismissing anyone else. Riker's side. Well, let's get busy on that EVA. LaForge, who do you see making the spacewalk? I think we only need two people. Since time is short, I prefer to have people who have already logged time in the Brom suit. Deanna Troy smiled at Riker. Since we need you and Data on the bridge, that leaves me and Jordi to go. Half an hour later, Deanna Troy was inside the bulky suit. She couldn't help but to remember the last time she had worn a Brom suit. During the awesome destruction of the planet Persephone V. The only reason she had been down during the height of the Genesis wave was to rescue Will and Data. This suit had done the job then, and it would do it again. Jordi LaForge gave her a thumbs up from his own white armor, and the two of them stepped awkwardly onto the transporter platform. Instantly Troy felt the relief of the wakelessness when she materialized in the low gravity. A few meters away floated a jet sled, a two-person conveyance with short-range thrusters. Both she and Jordy grabbed a handle. Jordy steered them into the debris field, a glittering ocean confetti that contained the ruins of two star ships framed by a massive black curtain. The immense rift made it seem as if they were falling into the blackest, deepest pit in the universe. As they cruised deeper into the debris, it was like riding a real sled through a golden snowstorm, and they sliced a tunnel through the glittering dust. The suits protected them, and so did Jordy's deft steering, but the visibility grew worse with every centimeter. LaForge's voice finally echoed in her ears. So what do you think? Troy looked around and couldn't even spot the rift or the enterprise thanks to the swirling cloud of debris. I think the chances of us seeing something in here are pretty remote, Jordy. Out of nowhere, a shape shot toward them like a torpedo, and Troy ducked as a horribly disfigured humanoid cruised past, his mouth agape and his eyes bulging. It was impossible to say what species he was or what propelled him past the rest of the space junk, but he was certainly dead. Jordy gasped in surprise. Wow. Should we try to recover the body? Troy shivered. Not now. Maybe on our way out. Can we get at the edges of this cloud where we can see what's coming? I don't want to stumble into that rift, and it may have some gravitational pull. After LaForge shot a few bursts, they were headed in what felt like an upward direction, although no such bearing was possible out here. Jordy, my radiation readouts are off the scale. Do you think we could even transport out of here? He didn't answer. He just continued to ride on the other side of the sled, one thickly gloved hand stuck in the handle. Troy pounded him on his shoulder, and he lost his grip and floated away, obviously unconscious. Troy saw a purple starfish-like creature latched on to his face plate, writhing and twitching. Then she realized that similar creatures littered the debris, grasping desperately with their tentacles. One of them struck a thruster on the sled, and Troy applied fuel and toasted it. Away, team, to transport a room one. Beam up LaForge immediately. Medical emergency. There was no response, except that a blackness surged over Troy's mind. The Antichoy felt a mixture of recognition and repulsion. There was no longer one entity in the rift, but billions and billions, all of them in a mindless stampede, trampling over each other to escape from the burning fires. At Gemworld, the overlying motives of the entity were controlled and revenge. Now it was just a mad yearning for survival. With a start, Deanna realized that the ruling entity of the other dimension was dead, and chaos ruled in its stead. This conclusion brought Troy to full consciousness. She had learned more than she needed to know. The rifts were like cracks in a dam, and when they exploded, there would be a flood of alien life and deadly radiation from one dimension into another. When she realized that she still had control of the sled, she carefully reversed the direction and soon had LaForge secured. Then she piloted the sled out of the shimmering cloud and back into view of the Enterprise and Javelick. She hailed the Enterprise. Transport a room, two to being back. In the engineering section of the Sequoia, Tesca walked past a bank of workstations, all devoted to parsing bajouren history, language and mythology, trying to find the planet mentioned cryptically in Vedic Yorka's announcement. She glanced over the shoulders of the researchers and saw one word occurring with considerable frequency. Machii. The Machii had been a rebellious group of Federation columnists who faced removal from their homes in the Demilitarized Zone due to an ill-fated treaty with the Cardassians. Battling both the Cardassians and the Federation, they fit the definition of allies to the bajourens. The Demilitarized Zone would be an ideal place for Yorka's showcase, so she had her researchers correlate the data with significant events which included the Machii, with a cross-check on dead planets. After that step, another name began to show up with some frequency on their screens. Solosos 3. Suddenly Admiral LaChiav strode purposefully into engineering. Tesca. Regimal just sent word that he's wracked his brain and he thinks that Solosos 3 could be it. A Starfleet effort to capture a Machii leader made the planet unlivable. Tesca nodded. Yes, firing quantum torpedoes with trilithium resin into the atmosphere was effective, but logically what can we do about an experiment on a dead planet in the Demilitarized Zone? The Chiav shook her head. Logically not very much, and Solosos 3 is only an educated guess. But I want to tell the Enterprise, then I'll get some sleep until we meet up with them. On the Enterprise, Picard strode down the corridor to the hatchway of the yacht, which was stowed under the saucer section. He was taking three other crew members, a pilot and two veteran security officers. If Kailina demanded a quest, some proof of his love, he could fulfill it. He had heard from Admiral LaChiav. Now he had a destination, Solosos 3, and his burning love would furnish the energy. A few moments later, a small, oblong craft took off from the underbelly of the saucer section, streaking away from the two gigantic starships and bursting into work.
description: In this episode of "The Genesis Wave" audiobook podcast, Tesca and Oswald encounter a human female named Linda Fini who was previously imprisoned in suspended animation. Through a mind meld, Tesca gains insight into her thoughts and helps Linda regain consciousness. They discover that they were part of an experiment to develop portable Genesys emitters for testing purposes and the missing shuttlecraft and passengers are likely responsible for the plant growth on Meldra 1. Admiral LaChayev orders them to investigate further, leading Tesca and Oswald towards a mission to prevent any further consequences from this mysterious event.

description: In this episode of "Star Trek: The Next Generation," John Von Vornholt narrates Tim Russ's performance in Genesis Force, an audiobook by Simon & Schuster Audio. The story unfolds with Ambassador Warff facing the daunting task of evacuating a Klingon outpost that is about to be destroyed on the Genesis planet. Despite his experience aboard the Enterprise being far from preparation for this grim work, Warff leads his troops through intense chaos as they evacuate hundreds of people and crew into shuttlecrafts that are nearly overwhelmed by the crowd's desperate wishes to escape. The episode captures the tension and urgency of their efforts, as well as the Klingon soldiers' bravery in face of overwhelming circumstances.
